//// helpers/createRule.d.ts
import type { RuleChecker, RuleOptions, RuleDefinition } from '../modules/validation';
/**
 * Creates a callable validation rule with typed parameters, debounce support,
 * and automatic error messages. The result is a stateless `RuleDefinition`:
 * calling it with parameters (`min(3)`, `min({ min: 3 })`) returns a configured
 * copy. The validation module compiles definitions into units and owns all
 * runtime state.
 *
 * Instance-independent by design: rules are authored at module scope, before
 * any `createVueform()` runs, so this produces plain descriptors and touches no
 * module, config or app.
 *
 * @param name The unique rule name used for lookup and message resolution.
 * @param check The validation function that returns `true`, `false`, or an
 *   error string.
 * @param options Optional configuration for params, debounce, typed messages,
 *   deps, and message overrides.
 */
export declare function createRule<const T extends readonly string[] | true = []>(name: string, check: RuleChecker<T>, options?: RuleOptions<T>): RuleDefinition<T>;

//// helpers/createVueform.d.ts
import { type App } from 'vue';
import { type UserConfig, type VueformConfig, type VueformGlobals, type VueformInstanceModules, type VueformModules } from './defineConfig';
import type { HttpInstance } from '../modules/http';
import type { ComponentNames } from '../types';
import type { VueformModule } from './defineModule';
import type { VueformPlugin } from './definePlugin';
import { useForm, type useModel } from '../composables';
import { type LocaleModule } from '../modules/locale';
declare module 'vue' {
    interface App {
        /**
         * Workaround for a Vue 3.5 + TS 5.8+ bug where `ObjectPlugin` does not
         * match the `Plugin` union in `app.use()`.
         */
        use(plugin: {
            install: (app: App, ...args: any[]) => any;
        }, ...options: any[]): this;
    }
}
/**
 * The merged component defaults of an instance: prop values keyed by component
 * name, layered from the config's `*`, `*element`, and per-component
 * `defaults`.
 */
export type VueformDefaults = Record<ComponentNames, Record<string, any>>;
/**
 * The object returned by `createVueform()`. Acts as a Vue plugin and exposes
 * helpers for registering modules/plugins and extracting CSS for SSR.
 */
export interface VueformInstance {
    /**
     * The instance's resolved configuration — the user's config merged with
     * defaults, same shape (`config.modules` holds the registered module
     * definitions).
     */
    readonly config: VueformConfig;
    /**
     * The modules created from `config.modules` at `createVueform()` — what
     * doorways and composables read. Module doorways and composables accept the
     * instance itself to resolve them outside a component context (e.g.
     * `getLocaleModule(vueform)`).
     */
    readonly modules: VueformInstanceModules;
    /**
     * The merged component defaults (`config.defaults` layered per component),
     * built lazily on first access.
     */
    readonly defaults: VueformDefaults;
    /**
     * The layout globals, extended by the config's and plugins' `globals` hooks,
     * built lazily on first access.
     */
    readonly globals: VueformGlobals;
    /**
     * The locale module (or its inert surface when not registered) — for code
     * outside components: `vueform.$locale.t('tag')`. Mirrors the component
     * context's `$locale`.
     */
    readonly $locale: LocaleModule;
    /**
     * An http instance bound to this Vueform instance (one per instance, own
     * interceptor scope) — for code outside components. Mirrors the component
     * context's `$http`; without the http module its requests reject.
     */
    readonly $http: HttpInstance;
    /**
     * `useModel` bound to this instance — for code with no component context:
     * stores, utilities, server code, module scope. Same signature and typing as
     * the `useModel` composable, which resolves the calling component's instance
     * instead.
     *
     * ```ts
     * import { vueform } from '@/vueform'
     * const model$ = vueform.useModel(schema, saved)
     * ```
     */
    readonly useModel: typeof useModel;
    /**
     * `useForm` bound to this instance — for code with no component context. Same
     * signature and typing as the `useForm` composable.
     */
    readonly useForm: typeof useForm;
    /**
     * Vue plugin install hook. Called automatically by `app.use()`.
     *
     * @param app The Vue application instance to install into.
     */
    readonly install: (app: App, ...options: any[]) => any;
    /**
     * Registers a module implementation before Vueform is installed. Throws if
     * called after installation.
     *
     * @param name The module key to register.
     * @param module The module implementation.
     */
    readonly module: <T extends keyof VueformModules>(name: T, module: NonNullable<VueformModules[T]>) => void;
    /**
     * Registers a Vueform plugin before installation. Throws if called after
     * installation.
     *
     * @param plugin The plugin to register.
     */
    readonly use: (plugin: VueformPlugin) => void;
    /**
     * Returns all generated CSS (grid + theme variables) for SSR or manual
     * injection.
     */
    readonly getCSS: () => string;
    /**
     * Returns a `<style>` tag for SSR injection covering both the grid layout and
     * theme variable declarations.
     */
    readonly getStyleTag: () => string;
}
/**
 * Creates a `createVueform` entry function around a set of default options.
 *
 * `TRequired` lists the modules the produced `createVueform` demands from its
 * caller. Bare entries that bundle nothing pass `<'model'>` — `model` has no
 * noop and must be registered. Theme entries that already register every module
 * pass none and get a fully optional argument.
 *
 * Structural CSS (the visual layer that consumes the token variables) is
 * expected to be loaded as a side effect by the adapter -- typically by the
 * adapter's theme file importing its SCSS entry. The factory itself only
 * injects the dynamic `:root { --vf-*: ... }` declarations derived from
 * `config.tokens`.
 *
 * @param defaultOptions The entry's default configuration.
 */
export declare function createVueformFactory<TRequired extends keyof VueformModules = never>(defaultOptions: UserConfig): (...args: [TRequired] extends [never] ? [config?: UserConfig] : [config: UserConfig & {
    modules: { [K in TRequired]-?: NonNullable<VueformModules[K]>; };
}]) => VueformInstance;
/**
 * Creates a Vueform Vue plugin instance from user-provided configuration merged
 * with the core defaults. Core bundles no modules or locales, so the `model`
 * module must be registered (everything else is optional and tree-shaken when
 * omitted).
 */
export declare const createVueform: (config: Partial<Omit<VueformConfig, "modules" | "build">> & {
    modules?: Partial<VueformModules> | undefined;
    build?: Partial<{
        styleId: string;
        scopedDarkMode: boolean;
        darkClass: string;
        lightClass: string;
    }> | undefined;
} & {
    modules: {
        model: VueformModule<import("@vueform/core").ModelModule>;
    };
}) => VueformInstance;

//// helpers/defineComputedSchema.d.ts
import { type ComputedRef } from 'vue';
import type { ArraySchema, ExactValidatedSchema, MatchesSchemaModel, ObjectSchema, StandardSchemaV1 } from '../types';
/**
 * `defineSchema` counterpart for reactive schemas: takes a getter and returns
 * it wrapped in a `computed`, so schemas built from reactive sources stay live
 * without a manual `computed(() => defineSchema({ … }))` wrapper. The same
 * validation and `const`-narrowing apply to the getter's return value.
 *
 * A separate function (instead of a `defineSchema` overload) so invalid schemas
 * keep reporting inline at the offending property — an overloaded
 * `defineSchema` collapses them into an aggregated "no overload matches" error
 * at the call site.
 *
 * The optional Standard Schema second argument works like `defineSchema`'s: it
 * is keyed on the returned computed ref (the getter produces a fresh object per
 * evaluation). Note the Standard Schema itself is static while the form schema
 * can change reactively.
 *
 * @param schema A getter producing the form schema from reactive sources.
 * @param validationSchema Optional Standard Schema validated against the whole
 *   form model, attached to the computed ref for automatic pickup.
 */
export declare function defineComputedSchema<const S extends (ObjectSchema | ArraySchema) & ExactValidatedSchema<S>, Z extends StandardSchemaV1 = StandardSchemaV1>(schema: () => S, validationSchema?: Z & MatchesSchemaModel<S, Z>): ComputedRef<S>;

    matrixTypes: {
        single: [string, string];
        multiple: [string, string];
        auto: [string, string];
    };
    /**
     * Whether to enable CSS grid layout.
     */
    grid: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether to inject styles via `@unhead/vue` when available.
     */
    useHead: boolean;
    /**
     * CSP nonce to apply to dynamically injected `<style>` tags.
     */
    nonce: string | undefined;
    /**
     * Named presets keyed by preset name.
     */
    presets: Record<string, PresetDefinition>;
    /**
     * Whether to enable class helper utilities.
     */
    classHelpers: boolean;
    /**
     * Function that generates class helper strings from keys.
     */
    classHelper: (key: string) => string;
    /**
     * The base theme: a complete token map (e.g. `origin` or `material` from
     * `@vueform/ui/themes`, or one produced by `extendTheme`). Replaces the
     * entry's baked-in theme wholesale — its `dark` block included — so passing a
     * theme to a pre-configured entry switches themes. `tokens` overrides are
     * then merged on top.
     */
    theme?: ThemeTokens;
    /**
     * Token overrides merged onto the base theme (the `theme` option, or the
     * entry's baked-in theme): top-level keys replace same-named tokens, and
     * `dark` blocks are shallow-merged (the `extendTheme` semantics). At runtime
     * this holds the fully resolved map — base theme plus overrides.
     */
    tokens: ThemeTokens;
    /**
     * Controls how dark mode is detected globally.
     *
     * - `'system'` (default) — follows OS preference via `prefers-color-scheme`.
     *   The CSS dark block is emitted inside a `@media` query.
     * - A CSS subselector string (e.g. `'.dark'`, `'[data-theme="dark"]'`) —
     *   watches `<html>` for that class or attribute. The CSS dark block is
     *   emitted as `:root<subselector> { ... }`.
     */
    darkMode?: DarkModeConfig;
    /**
     * Whether to lazily mount element slot content after idle callback. When
     * `false`, elements render their full template immediately without waiting
     * for `requestIdleCallback` or visibility. Default: `true`.
     */
    lazy: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether to use mobile-first (min-width) breakpoint logic.
     */
    mobileFirst: boolean;
    /**
     * Build-time options that control how Vueform emits assets.
     */
    build: {
        /**
         * The `id` attribute for the injected `<style>` tag. Defaults to
         * `'vueform-style'`.
         */
        styleId: string;
        /**
         * When `true`, generates additional scoped CSS blocks that re-declare all
         * theme tokens under `darkClass` and `lightClass`. This enables the `dark`
         * prop on `<VfForm>` to reliably toggle dark mode per-form regardless of
         * the environment. Disabled by default to avoid the extra CSS weight (~5–10
         * KB).
         */
        scopedDarkMode: boolean;
        /**
         * CSS class applied to forms with `dark={true}` when `scopedDarkMode` is
         * enabled. Defaults to `'vf-dark'`.
         */
        darkClass: string;
        /**
         * CSS class applied to forms with `dark={false}` when `scopedDarkMode` is
         * enabled. Defaults to `'vf-light'`.
         */
        lightClass: string;
    };
    /**
     * Whether plain-object prop values provided by the user are merged into
     * object values coming from blueprint defaults, config defaults, and presets.
     * When `false`, user-provided objects replace them entirely. Arrays always
     * replace regardless of this setting, and `classes`/`presets` keep their
     * dedicated merge semantics. Defaults to `true`.
     */
    mergeObjectProps?: boolean;
    /**
     * Default prop values per component, with `*` for all components and
     * `*element` for all elements.
     */
    defaults: ComponentDefaultsMap;
    /**
     * Per-key overrides for the shared element classes the element layout
     * installs (`root`, `label`, `errors`, …). A key you set replaces that key's
     * layout-provided value at the very bottom of the class chain — every other
     * key keeps the layout's default, and downstream overrides (presets, the
     * `classes`/`reclass` props) still apply on top. Static values given for
     * functional keys (e.g. `root`) are wrapped back into functions.
     */
    layoutClasses?: LayoutClassesMap;
    /**
     * Global class overrides per component, with `*` for all components and
     * `*element` for all elements. Functional class keys also accept a plain
     * `ClassValue`.
     */
    reclass: ComponentClassesMap;
    /**
     * Callback for custom globals initialization. Receives the same context as
     * plugins' `globals` hooks — the resolved `config` and a read-only view of
     * the `globals` accumulated so far. The returned members are merged into the
     * app's globals; returning a key that already exists overrides it with a dev
     * warning (silence with `globalWarns: false`).
     *
     * @param context The resolved configuration and the accumulated globals.
     */
    globals: (context: GlobalsHookContext) => Partial<VueformGlobals> | void;
    /**
     * Whether overriding an existing global from a `globals` hook (config or
     * plugin) logs a dev warning. Defaults to `true`.
     */
    globalWarns: boolean;
    /**
     * Unique ID generator for elements.
     */
    uid: () => UID;
    /**
     * Generates column CSS class names from size and breakpoint.
     *
     * @param size The column span (1–12).
     * @param breakpoint The breakpoint name.
     */
    cols: (size?: number, breakpoint?: string) => string;
    /**
     * Generates label layout CSS class names from size and breakpoint.
     *
     * @param size The label column span.
     * @param breakpoint The breakpoint name.
     */
    label: (size: number, breakpoint?: string) => string;
    /**
     * Resolves an icon name into a CSS class string for rendering.
     *
     * @param name The icon identifier.
     */
    icon: (name: string) => string;
    /**
     * Semantic icon names mapped to adapter-specific icon identifiers. Used to
     * resolve `$`-prefixed icon names (e.g. `$add`, `$remove`, `$sort`) so
     * built-in controls render the adapter's canonical icons. Mapped values are
     * passed through the `icon` resolver.
     */
    icons: Record<string, string>;
    /**
     * Regex pattern used to identify parameter placeholders in locale tag
     * strings. The pattern must contain a single capturing group that extracts
     * the parameter name. Defaults to `{(\w+)}` which matches `{param}` style
     * placeholders.
     */
    localeParamPattern: RegExp;
    /**
     * Generates locale tag keys for validation rule error messages.
     *
     * @param name The rule name.
     * @param type The value type variant.
     */
    ruleMessageTag: (name: string, type?: SizeTypes) => string;
}
/**
 * The user-facing partial configuration type where all keys are optional except
 * modules and build which are individually optional.
 */
export type UserConfig = PartialDeepKeys<VueformConfig, 'modules' | 'build'>;
/**
 * Type-safe helper for authoring Vueform configuration objects — an identity
 * function that only provides typing, like Vite's `defineConfig`.
 *
 * Use it for user configs passed to `createVueform` and for package default
 * configs handed to `createVueformFactory`. Both accept `UserConfig`;
 * completeness of the final config comes from merging entry defaults with the
 * modules each entry requires.
 *
 * @param config Partial Vueform configuration.
 */
export declare function defineConfig(config: UserConfig): UserConfig;

//// helpers/defineDefaults.d.ts
/**
 * Primitives and callables that may appear as literal prop defaults without a
 * factory wrapper.
 */
type NativeType = null | undefined | number | string | boolean | symbol | Function;
/**
 * Either a factory that receives props and returns the default, or a literal
 * value when it is a native type.
 */
type InferDefault<P, T> = ((props: P) => T & {}) | (T extends NativeType ? T : never);
/**
 * Maps each prop to an optional default expressed as a factory or a matching
 * native literal.
 */
export type InferDefaults<T> = {
    [K in keyof T]?: InferDefault<T, T[K]>;
};
/**
 * Returns a typed helper function for declaring component prop defaults
 * inferred from the given props type.
 *
 * Curried on purpose: TypeScript cannot partially infer remaining type
 * parameters, so `TProps` must be fixed in a first call while the defaults
 * object (and its precise `const` shape) is inferred in a second. A single
 * `defineDefaults<TProps>(…)` call would widen the return to
 * `InferDefaults<TProps>`, which breaks Vue `withDefaults` on generic SFCs.
 *
 * @private
 */
export declare function defineDefaults<TProps>(): <const TDefaults extends InferDefaults<TProps>>(defaults: TDefaults) => TDefaults;
/**
 * Returns blueprint defaults with the element `type` replaced by the
 * component's own element name (e.g. `'dropdown'`).
 *
 * Blueprint `defaults` bake in the blueprint's canonical type literal (e.g.
 * `'select'`), which a blueprint-reusing component cannot pass to
 * `withDefaults` — its `type` prop expects the component's own literal, at both
 * type level and runtime. The generic parameter keeps the literal inferred, so
 * no `as const` is needed at the call site.
 *
 * @private
 */
export declare function withType<TDefaults extends {
    type: string;
}, T extends string>(defaults: TDefaults, type: T): Omit<TDefaults, 'type'> & {
    type: T;
};
export {};

//// helpers/defineEvents.d.ts
import type { UnionToIntersection } from '../types';
/**
 * Converts a Vue emit declaration record into a map of event names to their
 * argument tuples, extracting rest-parameter types where available.
 */
export type TypeEmitsToOptions<T extends Record<string, any>> = {
    [K in keyof T & string]: T[K] extends [...args: infer Args] ? Args : any[];
};
/**
 * Registers or removes a callback for a specific event.
 */
export type EventListener<TEvents extends Record<string, any[]>> = <E extends keyof TEvents>(e: E, callback: (...args: TEvents[E]) => any) => void;
/**
 * Builds a `fire` signature from an event-name-to-argument-tuple map. Combines
 * per-event overloads (for typed arguments and autocomplete) with a union-name
 * guard signature so that a factory declaring an event name absent from the
 * blueprint's events is caught at compile time.
 */
export type FeatureFire<TEvents extends Record<string, any[]>> = UnionToIntersection<{
    [K in keyof TEvents & string]: (e: K, ...args: TEvents[K]) => any;
}[keyof TEvents & string]> & ((e: keyof TEvents & string, ...args: any[]) => any);
/**
 * Builds a listener registration signature (`on`, `off`, `onBefore`, `onAfter`)
 * from an event-name-to-argument-tuple map. Like `FeatureFire`, it combines
 * per-event overloads with a union-name guard so that a factory referencing an
 * event absent from the blueprint's events is caught at compile time.
 */
export type FeatureListener<TEvents extends Record<string, any[]>> = UnionToIntersection<{
    [K in keyof TEvents & string]: (e: K, callback: (...args: TEvents[K]) => any) => void;
}[keyof TEvents & string]> & ((e: keyof TEvents & string, callback: (...args: any[]) => any) => void);
/**
 * The events object a factory receives, typed from an event-name-to-argument
 * map. Each member is name-guarded so that referencing an event absent from the
 * blueprint's events fails to compile.
 */
export type FeatureEvents<TEvents extends Record<string, any[]>> = {
    /**
     * Fires an event with its typed arguments.
     */
    fire: FeatureFire<TEvents>;
    /**
     * Fires an event asynchronously, awaiting each callback and short-circuiting
     * when any returns `false`.
     */
    fireAsync: FeatureFire<TEvents>;
    /**
     * Subscribes a callback to an event.
     */
    on: FeatureListener<TEvents>;
    /**
     * Removes a previously registered event callback.
     */
    off: FeatureListener<TEvents>;
    /**
     * Registers a callback that runs before the main event listeners.
     */
    onBefore: FeatureListener<TEvents>;
    /**
     * Registers a callback that runs after the main event listeners.
     */
    onAfter: FeatureListener<TEvents>;
    /**
     * Whether any callback is currently registered for the given event, either
     * via `on` / `onBefore` / `onAfter` or as a component prop listener.
     */
    hasListeners?: (e: keyof TEvents & string) => boolean;
};
/**
 * The return type of `defineEvents`, providing fire, on, off, onBefore, and
 * onAfter methods.
 */
export type DefineEvents<T extends Record<string, any>> = ReturnType<typeof defineEvents<T>>;
/**
 * Creates a typed event system with synchronous and async firing, listener
 * registration, and before/after hooks.
 *
 * @private
 */
export declare function defineEvents<T extends Record<string, any>, TEvents extends TypeEmitsToOptions<T> = TypeEmitsToOptions<T>>(): {
    fire: <E extends keyof TEvents>(e: E, ...args: TEvents[E]) => void;
    fireAsync: <E extends keyof TEvents>(e: E, ...args: TEvents[E]) => Promise<any>;
    on: EventListener<TEvents>;
    off: EventListener<TEvents>;
    onBefore: EventListener<TEvents>;
    onAfter: EventListener<TEvents>;
    hasListeners: (e: keyof TEvents & string) => boolean;
    eventInProgress: import("vue").Ref<boolean, boolean>;
};

//// helpers/defineFeature.d.ts

 * `MakeXOptions` (or this type with concrete type args) unless the return type

 */
export type FeatureContext<Props extends Record<string, any> = Record<string, any>, Deps extends Record<string, any> = {}, Events = unknown> = {
    props: Props;
    deps: Deps;
    events: Events;
};

 * config.
 *

 */
export declare function defineFeature<C extends any, T extends Record<string, any>, R extends Record<string, any>>(factory: (config: C) => (options: T) => R): typeof factory;

//// helpers/defineModule.d.ts
import type { VueformInstance } from './createVueform';
import type { App } from 'vue';
/**
 * The context passed to a module's `create` hook when `createVueform()` creates
 * the registered module definitions' modules.
 */
export type ModuleCreateContext = {
    /**
     * The Vueform instance the module belongs to. Its resolved configuration is
     * `vueform.config` — the module's own options live under its `$key` (e.g.
     * `vueform.config.$http`). Modules that depend on other modules resolve them
     * through it lazily, at call time (`getLocaleModule(vueform)`) — never at
     * creation, so creation order is irrelevant.
     */
    vueform: VueformInstance;
};
/**
 * The context passed to a module's `install` hook when Vueform is installed
 * into a Vue app.
 */
export type ModuleInstallContext = {
    /**
     * The Vue application instance Vueform is being installed into.
     */
    app: App;
    /**
     * The Vueform instance being installed — its resolved configuration is
     * `vueform.config`.
     */
    vueform: VueformInstance;
};
/**
 * The context passed to a module's `getCSS` hook when the instance collects its
 * CSS (`vueform.getCSS()` / `vueform.getStyleTag()`).
 */
export type ModuleCSSContext = {
    /**
     * The Vueform instance whose CSS is being collected — its resolved
     * configuration is `vueform.config`.
     */
    vueform: VueformInstance;
};
/**
 * An optional Vueform capability registered via `createVueform({ modules })`.
 * Unregistered modules are tree-shaken (only their inert noop surfaces stay);
 * runtime code that depends on them degrades or throws at the point of use.
 *
 * `T` is the module's contract — a custom implementation is any definition
 * whose `create` returns a compliant module.
 */
export type VueformModule<T = unknown> = {
    /**
     * Creates the module. Called once per `createVueform()` at creation time (no
     * app involved); the result is stored on `vueform.modules` under the module's
     * key, while the definition itself stays in `config.modules`.
     *
     * @param context The creation context.
     */
    create: (context: ModuleCreateContext) => T;
    /**
     * Optional app-side effects (e.g. style injection), called once when Vueform
     * is installed into a Vue app.
     *
     * @param context The app install context.
     */
    install?: (context: ModuleInstallContext) => void;
    /**
     * Returns the CSS the module contributes (used by the theme module for SSR
     * style extraction).
     *
     * @param context The CSS collection context.
     */
    getCSS?: (context: ModuleCSSContext) => string;
};
/**
 * Defines a Vueform module. A typed identity helper — it does not transform the
 * definition at runtime.
 *
 * @private
 * @param module The module definition.
 */
export declare function defineModule<T>(module: VueformModule<T>): VueformModule<T>;

//// helpers/definePlugin.d.ts
import type { RawContextOf, PropsOf, ComponentNames, ElementNames, ComponentOptions, VueformComponent } from '../types';
import type { VueformInstance } from './createVueform';
import type { GlobalsHookContext, VueformConfig, VueformGlobals } from './defineConfig';
import type { DefineEvents } from './defineEvents';
import type { App, ComponentPropsOptions } from 'vue';
/**
 * Valid targets for a plugin's `apply` option, including component names,
 * wildcards, and pattern matchers.
 */
type PluginApplyName = ComponentNames | '*element' | '*' | RegExp | (string & {});
/**
 * The context passed to a plugin's `install` hook when Vueform is installed
 * into a Vue app — the same shape a module's `install` hook receives.
 */
export type PluginInstallContext = {
    /**
     * The Vue application instance Vueform is being installed into.
     */
    app: App;
    /**
     * The Vueform instance being installed — its resolved configuration is
     * `vueform.config`.
     */
    vueform: VueformInstance;
};
/**
 * The normalized plugin shape used internally by Vueform after processing
 * plugin options.
 */
export type VueformPlugin = {
    name?: string;
    apply?: string | RegExp | ((component: VueformComponent) => boolean) | (string | RegExp)[];
    props?: ComponentPropsOptions;
    emits?: string[];
    plugins?: VueformPlugin[];
    extend?: (props: any, api: any) => void | Record<string, any>;
    config?: (config: any) => void;
    globals?: (context: {
        config: any;
        globals: Readonly<Partial<VueformGlobals>>;
    }) => Partial<VueformGlobals> | void;
    /**
     * App-side effects run once when the instance is installed into a Vue app
     * (after components are registered) — e.g. registering a directive.
     */
    install?: (context: PluginInstallContext) => void;
};
/**
 * Typed options for defining a Vueform plugin, with component targeting via
 * `$apply`.
 */
export type VueformPluginOptions<T extends PluginApplyName> = {
    name?: string;
    apply?: T | ReadonlyArray<T>;
    props?: ComponentPropsOptions;
    emits?: string[];
    plugins?: VueformPlugin[];
    extend?: (props: Readonly<T extends '*' | RegExp ? PropsOf<ComponentNames> : T extends '*element' ? PropsOf<ElementNames> : T extends ComponentNames ? PropsOf<T> : any>, api: (T extends '*' | RegExp ? RawContextOf<ComponentNames> : T extends '*element' ? RawContextOf<ElementNames> : T extends ComponentNames ? RawContextOf<T> : any) & DefineEvents<any>) => void | Record<string, any>;
    config?: (config: VueformConfig) => void;
    globals?: (context: GlobalsHookContext) => Partial<VueformGlobals> | void;
    install?: (context: PluginInstallContext) => void;
};
/**
 * Plugin options variant where `apply` is a predicate function for custom
 * component matching.
 */
export type VueformPluginOptionsWithApplyFn = {
    name?: string;
    props?: ComponentPropsOptions;
    emits?: string[];
    plugins?: VueformPlugin[];
    apply: (component: ComponentOptions) => boolean;
    extend?: (props: any, api: any) => void | Record<string, any>;
    config?: (config: VueformConfig) => void;
    globals?: (context: GlobalsHookContext) => Partial<VueformGlobals> | void;
    install?: (context: PluginInstallContext) => void;
};
/**
 * A plugin factory returned by `definePlugin()`. Every plugin is a function:
 * calling it — with options when the plugin takes any — produces the plugin
 * object passed to the `plugins` config option or `vueform.use()`.
 */
export type VueformPluginFactory<Args extends unknown[] = []> = (...args: Args) => VueformPlugin;
/**
 * Defines a Vueform plugin that can extend components, config, and globals.
 *
 * Takes a factory producing the plugin's definition — its parameters become the
 * plugin's options — and returns the plugin as a callable factory, so
 * registration is uniform whether or not the plugin takes options: `plugins:
 * [myPlugin()]` or `plugins: [myPlugin({ ... })]`.
 *
 * @param definition A factory producing the plugin's definition — target
 *   components, props, emits, and lifecycle hooks — from the plugin's options.
 */
export declare function definePlugin<Args extends unknown[], T extends PluginApplyName>(definition: (...args: Args) => VueformPluginOptions<T>): VueformPluginFactory<Args>;
export declare function definePlugin<Args extends unknown[]>(definition: (...args: Args) => VueformPluginOptionsWithApplyFn): VueformPluginFactory<Args>;
export {};

//// helpers/defineSchema.d.ts
import type { ArraySchema, ExactValidatedSchema, MatchesSchemaModel, ObjectSchema, StandardSchemaV1 } from '../types';
/**
 * Keys a Standard Schema to a schema object or ref in the shared side-table,
 * for `getAttachedValidationSchema` to find. Internal plumbing shared with
 * `defineComputedSchema`.
 *
 * @private
 */
export declare function attachValidationSchema(schema: object, validationSchema: StandardSchemaV1): void;
/**
 * Returns the Standard Schema attached to a schema (or schema ref) via
 * `defineSchema` / `defineComputedSchema`'s second argument, if any. For refs
 * the ref itself is tried first, then the unwrapped schema object. Lookups go
 * through `toRaw` since schemas passed as props arrive as reactive proxies
 * while the WeakMap is keyed by the original object.
 *
 * @private
 * @param schema The schema object or ref to look up.
 */
export declare function getAttachedValidationSchema(schema: unknown): StandardSchemaV1 | undefined;
/**
 * Identity helper that validates and `const`-narrows a form schema so it can
 * drive type-level features (`SchemaToModel`, typed `find()` paths, …).
 *
 * Each entry is validated against its registered element's props — including
 * prop-driven model narrowing, so e.g. `items` / `itemValue` constrain
 * `modelValue` / `default`, `itemValue` / `itemLabel` / `groupChildren` (and
 * PrimeVue `optionValue` / `optionLabel` / `optionGroupChildren`, …) are
 * checked against the `items` / `options` shape, and `translate: true` requires
 * a locale-keyed `modelValue`. Nested `schema` objects/arrays are validated
 * recursively.
 *
 * An optional Standard Schema (Zod, Valibot, ArkType, …) can be passed as the
 * second argument for form-level (cross-field) validation. Its inferred input
 * type is checked against the schema's model type at compile time, and it is
 * attached to the schema object so forms and models using this schema pick it
 * up automatically — no need to pass it again.
 *
 * @param schema The form schema in object or array notation.
 * @param validationSchema Optional Standard Schema validated against the whole
 *   form model, attached to the schema for automatic pickup.
 */
export declare function defineSchema<const S extends (ObjectSchema | ArraySchema) & ExactValidatedSchema<S>, Z extends StandardSchemaV1 = StandardSchemaV1>(schema: S, validationSchema?: Z & MatchesSchemaModel<S, Z>): S;

//// helpers/defineSlot.d.ts
import { type ComponentPublicInstance, type VNodeChild } from 'vue';
import type { SlotProps } from '../types';
/**
 * Readonly map from selected slot prop names to their types for the given
 * component and slot.
 */
type PropOptions<C extends keyof SlotProps, S extends keyof SlotProps[C], P extends (keyof SlotProps[C][S])[]> = Readonly<{
    [K in P[number]]: SlotProps[C][S][K];
}>;
/**
 * Component options accepted by `defineSlot`, with the `setup` first argument
 * and Options API `this` narrowed to only the declared props.
 */
type SlotOptions<C extends keyof SlotProps, S extends keyof SlotProps[C], P extends (keyof SlotProps[C][S])[]> = {
    props?: P;
    setup?: (props: PropOptions<C, S, P>) => (() => VNodeChild) | Record<string, unknown>;
    template?: string;
    render?: (this: PropOptions<C, S, P>) => VNodeChild;
    components?: Record<string, unknown>;
    [key: string]: unknown;
} & ThisType<ComponentPublicInstance<PropOptions<C, S, P>>>;
/**
 * Defines a typed slot component for a specific Vueform component slot with
 * type-safe props.
 *
 * @param path The host component and slot, as `VfName.slotName`.
 * @param options Vue component options including the list of slot props to
 *   receive.
 */
export declare function defineSlot<C extends keyof SlotProps & string, S extends keyof SlotProps[C] & string, P extends (keyof SlotProps[C][S])[] = []>(_path: `${C}.${S}`, options: SlotOptions<C, S, P>): import("vue").Raw<import("vue").DefineComponent<{}, {}, {}, {}, {}, import("vue").ComponentOptionsMixin, import("vue").ComponentOptionsMixin, {}, string, import("vue").PublicProps, Readonly<{}> & Readonly<{}>, {}, {}, {}, {}, string, import("vue").ComponentProvideOptions, true, {}, any>>;
export {};

//// helpers/defineTheme.d.ts
/**
 * Type-safe helper for authoring a theme with your own token structure —
 * arbitrary keys are accepted, so use it when you are building a custom visual
 * layer whose stylesheets define their own token vocabulary. The one universal
 * contract it enforces is an explicit `dark` block (pass `{}` to opt out of a
 * dark variant).
 *
 * To author a theme for an adapter's existing token structure, use the
 * `defineTheme` exported from that adapter's `/themes` entry instead — it
 * enforces the adapter's complete key set and registers the token type
 * augmentation.
 *
 * @param theme The theme definition.
 */
export declare function defineTheme<T extends {
    dark: Record<string, string | number>;
} & Record<string, unknown>>(theme: T): T;

//// helpers/extendTheme.d.ts
import type { InferThemeTokens } from '../types';
/**
 * Produces a new theme object by layering overrides on top of an existing
 * theme. Non-`dark` keys replace same-named tokens at the top level. The `dark`
 * override is shallow-merged with the base's `dark`.
 *
 * The base object is not mutated.
 *
 * @param base The token map to extend (typically `origin` or another
 *   `defineTheme` result).
 * @param overrides Token overrides — keyed by the base theme's tokens, custom
 *   keys accepted.
 */
export declare function extendTheme<TBase extends Record<string, any>>(base: TBase, overrides: InferThemeTokens<TBase>): TBase;

//// helpers/resolveAddon.d.ts
import type { SecurityModule } from '../modules/security';
import type { AddonItem } from '../types';
/**
 * A resolved addon value: display text (rendered escaped by the addon
 * component, so it needs no sanitization), or a dynamic component descriptor
 * (`{ component, props }`) for schema addons.
 */
export type ResolvedAddon = string | {
    component: string;
    props: Record<string, any>;
} | undefined;
/**
 * Modules `resolveAddon` needs from the caller's setup context — gather them
 * via `useLocale()`, `useSecurity()`, and `useExpression()`.
 */
export interface ResolveAddonModules {
    localize: (value: any) => any;
    expression: {
        allowed: (scope: string) => boolean;
        resolve: (value: string) => any;
    };
}
/**
 * Resolves a raw `AddonItem` into a text string (localized and
 * expression-resolved; rendered escaped downstream) or a dynamic component
 * descriptor — the resolution the addon blueprint performs, exposed for layout
 * components that render addons without a dedicated addon component.
 *
 * @private
 */
export declare function resolveAddon(addon: AddonItem | undefined, { localize, expression }: ResolveAddonModules, { $security, }: {
    $security: Pick<SecurityModule, 'allowsComponent' | 'sanitizeProps'>;
}): ResolvedAddon;

export declare function resolveModules(vueform?: VueformInstance): VueformInstanceModules;

import type { VueformInstance } from './createVueform';

export declare function resolveVueform(vueform?: VueformInstance): VueformInstance;

//// modules/autosave/createAutosave.d.ts
import type { VueformInstance } from '../../helpers';
import type { AutosaveModule } from './types';
/**
 * Creates an autosave instance from the given app config (`$autosave` is
 * currently reserved). The returned module's `makeAutosave` wires one form's
 * autosave behavior: remote saves to `endpoint` on the configured events and
 * interval (deferred while the form is invalid unless `invalid: true` — a
 * skipped save runs when the form becomes valid), and a `local` draft mirror
 * that saves the model to storage on every action, loads it back on mount, and
 * clears it on successful submit.
 *
 * @param vueform The Vueform instance; its config (`$autosave` is reserved;
 *   `$security` is peeked at to warn when local drafts would be stored without
 *   any cipher).
 */
export declare function createAutosave(vueform: VueformInstance): AutosaveModule;

//// modules/autosave/definition.d.ts
/**
 * The autosave module. Register via `createVueform({ modules: { autosave } })`.
 */
export declare const autosave: import("../../helpers").VueformModule<import("@vueform/core").AutosaveModule>;

//// modules/autosave/index.d.ts
export { autosave } from './definition';
export * from './module';
export * from './types';

//// modules/autosave/module.d.ts
import type { VueformInstance } from '../../helpers';
import type { AutosaveModule } from './types';
/**
 * Returns the resolved instance's autosave module, or the inert `noopAutosave`
 * surface (the `autosave` prop has no effect, context methods no-op) when the
 * `autosave` module is not registered. Resolves the explicit `vueform` (a
 * `createVueform()` instance or config) when given, otherwise the config
 * injected by the calling component's app.
 */
export declare function getAutosaveModule(vueform?: VueformInstance): AutosaveModule;
/**
 * Whether a autosave module is registered — `false` means `getAutosaveModule`
 * serves the inert `noopAutosave` surface.
 */
export declare function hasAutosaveModule(vueform?: VueformInstance): boolean;

//// modules/autosave/noop.d.ts
import type { AutosaveModule } from './types';
/**
 * The inert autosave surface used when the `autosave` module is not registered
 * — the `autosave` prop has no effect (with a one-time dev warning when it is
 * set) and the form context methods (`autosave`, `clearAutosaved`,
 * `loadAutosaved`) are no-ops.
 */
export declare const noopAutosave: AutosaveModule;

//// modules/autosave/types.d.ts
import type { HttpError, HttpResponse, RequestMethod } from '../http';
import type { EndpointHandler } from '../../types';
import type { ComputedRef, Ref } from 'vue';
/**
 * Global options for the autosave module (the `$autosave` config object).
 */
export interface AutosaveModuleOptions {
}
/**
 * Trigger options for the form's autosave behavior.
 */
export type AutosaveOnOptions = 'change' | 'next' | 'back' | 'step' | 'tab';
/**
 * Prop type specifying which events trigger autosave.
 */
export type AutosaveOnProp = (AutosaveOnOptions | (string & {}))[];
/**
 * A storage backend for local autosave — the `localStorage` slice of the Web
 * Storage API, so `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, and custom adapters all
 * qualify.
 */
export type AutosaveStorage = {
    getItem: (key: string) => string | null;
    setItem: (key: string, value: string) => void;
    removeItem: (key: string) => void;
};
/**
 * Configuration of the local half of autosave. `true` enables it with the
 * defaults (`localStorage` under a key derived from the form's `name`).
 */
export type AutosaveLocalProp = boolean | {
    /**
     * The storage key. Defaults to `vueform:{form name}` — without a key or a
     * form `name`, local autosave is disabled with a dev warning.
     */
    key?: string;
    /**
     * The storage backend. Defaults to `localStorage`.
     */
    storage?: AutosaveStorage;
    /**
     * Whether a stored draft is loaded back into the form on mount. Defaults
     * to `true`. When `false`, drafts can still be loaded manually via
     * `loadAutosaved()`.
     */
    load?: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether the stored draft is cleared on successful submit. Defaults to
     * `true`.
     */
    clear?: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether the app-level `$security` cipher is applied to this form's
     * draft. Defaults to `true` — and storing drafts with no cipher
     * configured warns in dev: plaintext drafts must be a conscious choice.
     * Set `false` to knowingly store this form's draft as plaintext (and
     * silence the warning); registering identity `$security` ciphers is the
     * app-wide equivalent.
     */
    encrypt?: boolean;
};
/**
 * Configuration object of the form's autosave behavior, covering the remote
 * endpoint, the local draft mirror, and the remote scheduling options.
 */
export type AutosaveProp<TContext = any> = {
    /**
     * The remote target — an endpoint URL (expressions are resolved) or an async
     * handler function.
     */
    endpoint?: string | EndpointHandler<TContext>;
    /**
     * The HTTP method for endpoint requests. Defaults to `'POST'`.
     */
    method?: RequestMethod;
    /**
     * The local draft mirror. Saves the form's model to storage on every action
     * (change and page navigation, undebounced and regardless of validity), loads
     * it back on mount (`load: false` to disable), and clears it on successful
     * submit (`clear: false` to keep it).
     */
    local?: AutosaveLocalProp;
    /**
     * Form events that trigger a remote save (e.g. `change`, `next`, `step`,
     * `tab`). Any form event name is accepted. Defaults to `['change']` — the
     * form saves shortly after its data changes.
     */
    on?: AutosaveOnProp;
    /**
     * Interval in milliseconds for periodic remote saves on a fixed schedule. The
     * timer fires regardless of the last save's outcome, so it also retries after
     * failed saves. Defaults to `0` (no timer).
     */
    interval?: number;
    /**
     * Debounce delay in milliseconds applied when `on` includes `'change'`.
     * Defaults to `1000`.
     */
    delay?: number;
    /**
     * Whether remote saves are sent while the form is invalid. Defaults to
     * `false` — a save triggered while the form is invalid is deferred and runs
     * as soon as the form becomes valid.
     */
    invalid?: boolean;
    /**
     * Further transforms the data a remote save sends. Receives the form's
     * payload (with `transformPayload` already applied) and returns the data to
     * send. Local drafts are unaffected.
     */
    transform?: (data: Record<string, any>, context$: TContext) => Record<string, any>;
};
/**
 * Configuration options for `makeAutosave`, wiring one form's autosave
 * behavior.
 */
export type MakeAutosaveOptions = {
    /**
     * The autosave configuration object. When undefined, autosave is disabled.
     */
    autosave: Ref<AutosaveProp | undefined>;
    /**
     * The form's submission payload (with `transformPayload` applied).
     */
    payload: ComputedRef<Record<string, any>>;
    /**
     * The form's raw model data (before any form-level transform).
     */
    model: Ref<Record<string, any>>;
    /**
     * Data paths of elements marked `sensitive` — their values are stripped from
     * locally stored drafts.
     */
    sensitivePaths: ComputedRef<string[]>;
    /**
     * Custom HTTP headers to include in autosave requests.
     */
    headers: Ref<Record<string, string> | undefined>;
    /**
     * Whether to send autosave data as JSON instead of FormData.
     */
    json: Ref<boolean | undefined>;
    /**
     * Whether to encode file uploads as base64 in autosave requests.
     */
    base64: Ref<boolean | undefined>;
    /**
     * Whether the form is currently invalid. Unless the autosave config sets
     * `invalid: true`, remote saves are skipped while this is `true`.
     */
    invalid: ComputedRef<boolean>;
    /**
     * The form's `name` prop, used as the default local storage key.
     */
    name: Ref<string | undefined>;
    /**
     * Loads data into the form's model (used to restore local drafts).
     */
    load: (data: Record<string, any>) => void;
    /**
     * The form's component context, passed to handlers and events.
     */
    form$: any;
    /**
     * Resolves expressions in a string endpoint URL (when allowed for the
     * `autosave` prop key).
     */
    resolveEndpoint: (url: string) => string;
    /**
     * Fires a form event synchronously.
     */
    fire: {
        /**
         * Fires the autosaveSuccess event after a successful save request.
         *
         * @param e The event name.
         * @param response The HTTP response from the autosave request.
         * @param form$ The form context.
         */
        (e: 'autosaveSuccess', response: HttpResponse, form$: any): any;
        /**
         * Fires the autosaveFail event after a failed save request.
         *
         * @param e The event name.
         * @param error The HTTP error that caused the failure.
         * @param form$ The form context.
         */
        (e: 'autosaveFail', error: HttpError, form$: any): any;
    };
    /**
     * Fires a form event asynchronously, awaiting each callback. Returns `false`
     * if any handler cancels, or the last non-undefined return value.
     */
    fireAsync: {
        /**
         * Fires the autosave pre-hook event before the remote request is sent.
         *
         * @param e The event name.
         * @param data The form data to be autosaved.
         * @param form$ The form context.
         */
        (e: 'autosave', data: Record<string, any>, form$: any): Promise<any>;
        /**
         * Fires the autosaveRestore pre-hook event before a stored draft is loaded
         * back into the form.
         *
         * @param e The event name.
         * @param data The stored draft data about to be restored.
         * @param form$ The form context.
         */
        (e: 'autosaveRestore', data: Record<string, any>, form$: any): Promise<any>;
    };
    /**
     * Subscribes a callback to a form event.
     *
     * @param e The event name to listen for.
     * @param callback The handler to invoke when the event fires.
     */
    on: (e: any, callback: (...args: any[]) => any) => any;
    /**
     * Unsubscribes a callback from a form event.
     *
     * @param e The event name to stop listening for.
     * @param callback The handler to remove.
     */
    off: (e: any, callback: (...args: any[]) => any) => any;
};
/**
 * One form's wired autosave behavior: the manual trigger and the local draft
 * methods, exposed on the form's context.
 */
export type AutosaveInstance = {
    /**
     * Performs an autosave immediately: writes the local draft (when `local` is
     * configured) and runs the remote save (when `endpoint` is configured). The
     * validity gate applies as configured; pass `invalid` to override the
     * config's `invalid` prop for this one call — `true` sends even while the
     * form is invalid, `false` enforces the gate. A gated call while the form is
     * invalid still writes the local draft and defers the remote save.
     *
     * @param options Per-call overrides (`invalid`).
     */
    autosave: (options?: {
        invalid?: boolean;
    }) => Promise<void>;
    /**
     * Removes the locally stored draft, if any.
     */
    clearAutosaved: () => void;
    /**
     * Loads the stored draft into the form, resolving whether a draft was found
     * and loaded (async because a configured `$security.decrypt` may be). Unlike
     * the automatic load on mount, a manual call fires no `autosaveRestore`
     * pre-hook — calling it _is_ the consent.
     */
    loadAutosaved: () => Promise<boolean>;
};
/**
 * The autosave module: wires interval, event, and local-draft saving for a form
 * from its `autosave` configuration object.
 */
export interface AutosaveModule {
    /**
     * Wires a form's autosave behavior from the given options. Must be called
     * within a component setup context (registers lifecycle hooks and watchers).
     *
     * @param options The form-specific autosave wiring options.
     */
    makeAutosave: (options: MakeAutosaveOptions) => AutosaveInstance;
}

//// modules/conditions/createConditions.d.ts
import { type MaybeRef, type Ref } from 'vue';
import type { VueformInstance } from '../../helpers';
import type { FormContext } from '../../types';
import type { ConditionsModule, ConditionsTriggerProp } from './types';
interface ConditionRelativeOperands {
    '>': string | number;
    '>=': string | number;
    '<': string | number;
    '<=': string | number;
    '==': string | number | boolean | null | undefined | Array<string | number | boolean | undefined | null>;
    '!=': string | number | boolean | null | undefined | Array<string | number | boolean | undefined | null>;
    between: [string | number, string | number];
    in: Array<string | number>;
    not_in: Array<string | number>;
    before: 'today' | string;
    after: 'today' | string;
    '^': string | number;
    $: string | number;
    '*': string | number;
}
type StructuredCondition = readonly [string, 'empty' | 'not_empty' | 'today'] | {
    [K in keyof ConditionRelativeOperands]: readonly [
        string,
        K,
        ConditionRelativeOperands[K]
    ];
}[keyof ConditionRelativeOperands];
export type RawConditionsProp<TContext = any> = string | boolean | Ref<boolean> | ((context$: TContext) => boolean | Promise<boolean>) | readonly StructuredCondition[] | readonly (readonly StructuredCondition[])[];
export type NegatedConditionsProp<TContext = any> = {
    not: RawConditionsProp<TContext>;
};
export interface MakeConditionalOptions {
    path?: MaybeRef<string>;
    debounce?: MaybeRef<number | undefined>;
    trigger?: MaybeRef<ConditionsTriggerProp | undefined>;
    valueFormat?: MaybeRef<string | undefined>;
    form$?: FormContext;
}
/**
 * Creates a conditions instance. Date comparisons resolve their adapter via the
 * config's date module and expression conditions resolve through the config's
 * expression module.
 *
 * @param vueform The owning instance (uses `$conditions.strict` /
 *   `$conditions.debounce`).
 */
export declare function createConditions(vueform: VueformInstance): ConditionsModule;
export {};

import type { ConditionsModule } from './types';

 * resolves as met, lists resolve to no per-item evaluations.

export declare const noopConditions: ConditionsModule;

//// modules/conditions/types.d.ts
import { type MaybeRef, type Ref } from 'vue';
import type { MakeConditionalOptions, NegatedConditionsProp, RawConditionsProp } from './createConditions';
/**
 * The full conditions prop type accepted by component props, supporting raw or
 * negated conditions.
 *
 * `TContext` defaults to `any` for schema / blueprint use; component prop
 * interfaces specialize it (same pattern as event `context$`).
 */
export type ConditionalProp<TContext = any> = RawConditionsProp<TContext> | NegatedConditionsProp<TContext>;
/**
 * Conditions produced by a function (`colConditions`, `itemConditions`, …).
 * Function returns get no contextual typing through `defineSchema`'s generic
 * inference, so structured array literals arrive widened (`string[][]`, not
 * tuple arrays) — the widened shape is accepted and the runtime validates
 * structure, as it already does. Declarative conditions props stay on the
 * strict `ConditionalProp`.
 */
export type ConditionsResult<TContext = any> = ConditionalProp<TContext> | readonly (readonly unknown[])[];
/**
 * The accepted forms of the `conditions-trigger` prop, used as the single watch
 * source that drives re-evaluation of a component's async conditional props. An
 * array of element paths watches those elements' values, a `Ref` watches the
 * ref, and a function is used as a Vue watch getter. When omitted, the trigger
 * defaults to any change in the model.
 */
export type ConditionsTriggerProp<TContext = any> = string[] | Ref<any> | ((context$: TContext) => any);
/**
 * Global options for the conditions module (the `$conditions` config object).
 */
export interface ConditionsModuleOptions {
    /**
     * Whether to use strict comparisons when evaluating structured conditions.
     * Defaults to `false`.
     */
    strict?: boolean;
    /**
     * The debounce delay in milliseconds applied before re-evaluating async
     * conditional props when their trigger source changes. Defaults to `300`.
     */
    debounce?: number;
}
/**
 * The conditions module type providing model-bound condition evaluation.
 */
export interface ConditionsModule {
    /**
     * Resolves a single conditional prop into a boolean ref evaluated against the
     * given model.
     *
     * @param conditions The raw conditional value (or a ref/getter to it).
     * @param model The model conditions are checked against.
     * @param context$ The component context passed to function conditions.
     * @param options Path, debounce, trigger, and date format options.
     */
    makeConditional: (conditions: MaybeRef<ConditionsResult | undefined>, model: MaybeRef<Record<string, any> | undefined>, context$: any, options?: MakeConditionalOptions) => Ref<boolean>;
    /**
     * Resolves conditions for a dynamic list of items into a parallel array of
     * boolean refs, managed inside an effect scope that is rebuilt whenever the
     * source list changes. Items without conditions default to `true`.
     *
     * @param source A ref or getter returning the list of items.
     * @param getConditions Extracts the conditions prop from each item.
     * @param model The model conditions are checked against.
     * @param context$ The component context passed to function conditions.
     * @param options Path, debounce, trigger, and date format options.
     */
    makeConditionalList: <T>(source: Ref<T[]>, getConditions: (item: T) => ConditionsResult | undefined, model: MaybeRef<Record<string, any> | undefined>, context$: any, options?: MakeConditionalOptions) => Ref<Ref<boolean>[]>;
}

//// modules/date/types.d.ts
/**
 * Supported date unit identifiers (singular and plural forms).
 */
export type DateUnit = 'year' | 'month' | 'week' | 'day' | 'hour' | 'minute' | 'second' | 'millisecond' | 'years' | 'months' | 'weeks' | 'days' | 'hours' | 'minutes' | 'seconds' | 'milliseconds';
/**
 * /** A date wrapper providing a dayjs-compatible API for parsing,
 * manipulation, comparison, and formatting.
 */
export interface DateInstance {
    /**
     * Returns whether the underlying date is valid.
     */
    isValid(): boolean;
    /**
     * Returns the full year (e.g. 2025).
     */
    year(): number;
    /**
     * Returns the month (1–12).
     */
    month(): number;
    /**
     * Returns the day of the month (1–31).
     */
    date(): number;
    /**
     * Returns the day of the week (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday).
     */
    day(): number;
    /**
     * Returns the hour (0–23).
     */
    hour(): number;
    /**
     * Returns the minute (0–59).
     */
    minute(): number;
    /**
     * Returns the second (0–59).
     */
    second(): number;
    /**
     * Returns the millisecond (0–999).
     */
    millisecond(): number;
    /**
     * Returns a new instance with the given amount added.
     *
     * @param amount The quantity to add.
     * @param unit The date unit to add.
     */
    add(amount: number, unit: DateUnit): DateInstance;
    /**
     * Returns a new instance with the given amount subtracted.
     *
     * @param amount The quantity to subtract.
     * @param unit The date unit to subtract.
     */
    subtract(amount: number, unit: DateUnit): DateInstance;
    /**
     * Returns a new instance set to the start of the given unit.
     *
     * @param unit The date unit whose start boundary to snap to.
     */
    startOf(unit: DateUnit): DateInstance;
    /**
     * Returns a new instance set to the end of the given unit.
     *
     * @param unit The date unit whose end boundary to snap to.
     */
    endOf(unit: DateUnit): DateInstance;
    /**
     * Returns a new instance with the specified unit set to a value.
     *
     * @param unit The date unit to set.
     * @param value The numeric value to assign.
     */
    set(unit: DateUnit, value: number): DateInstance;
    /**
     * Returns whether this date is before the other date.
     *
     * @param other The date to compare against.
     * @param granularity Optional unit granularity for the comparison.
     */
    isBefore(other: DateInstance, granularity?: DateUnit): boolean;
    /**
     * Returns whether this date is after the other date.
     *
     * @param other The date to compare against.
     * @param granularity Optional unit granularity for the comparison.
     */
    isAfter(other: DateInstance, granularity?: DateUnit): boolean;
    /**
     * Returns whether this date is the same as the other date.
     *
     * @param other The date to compare against.
     * @param granularity Optional unit granularity for the comparison.
     */
    isSame(other: DateInstance, granularity?: DateUnit): boolean;
    /**
     * Returns whether this date is the same as or before the other date.
     *
     * @param other The date to compare against.
     * @param granularity Optional unit granularity for the comparison.
     */
    isSameOrBefore(other: DateInstance, granularity?: DateUnit): boolean;
    /**
     * Returns whether this date is the same as or after the other date.
     *
     * @param other The date to compare against.
     * @param granularity Optional unit granularity for the comparison.
     */
    isSameOrAfter(other: DateInstance, granularity?: DateUnit): boolean;
    /**
     * Returns whether this date falls between two other dates.
     *
     * @param start The range start date.
     * @param end The range end date.
     * @param granularity Optional unit granularity for the comparison.
     * @param inclusivity Bracket notation controlling boundary inclusion.
     */
    isBetween(start: DateInstance, end: DateInstance, granularity?: DateUnit, inclusivity?: '()' | '[)' | '(]' | '[]'): boolean;
    /**
     * Returns the difference between this date and another in the given unit.
     *
     * @param other The date to diff against.
     * @param unit The unit for the result (milliseconds if omitted).
     */
    diff(other: DateInstance, unit?: DateUnit): number;
    /**
     * Returns the underlying native `Date` object (cloned).
     */
    toDate(): Date;
    /**
     * Returns the date as an ISO 8601 string with time and timezone.
     */
    toISOString(): string;
    /**
     * Returns the date as an ISO 8601 date-only string (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
     */
    toISODate(): string;
    /**
     * Returns the date as a Unix timestamp in milliseconds.
     */
    valueOf(): number;
    /**
     * Returns the date as a Unix timestamp in seconds.
     */
    unix(): number;
    /**
     * Returns a deep copy of this date instance.
     */
    clone(): DateInstance;
    /**
     * Formats the date using the given format string. Requires a date format
     * plugin (`@vueform/date-dayjs`, `@vueform/date-fns`, or
     * `@vueform/date-luxon`).
     *
     * @param formatString The format pattern.
     */
    format(formatString: string): string;
}
/**
 * The date module instance: a factory capturing the configured adapter. `make`
 * parses a value into a `DateInstance`. Per-call state lives in the returned
 * instance, not the module.
 */
export interface DateModule {
    /**
     * Parses a value into a `DateInstance`, returning the current date when
     * called without arguments.
     *
     * @param value The date value to parse.
     * @param format Optional format string (requires a date format plugin).
     */
    make: (value?: any, format?: string) => DateInstance;
}
/**
 * A factory that produces the date module's `make` function from the module
 * options (`config.$date`).
 */
export type DateAdapter = (options?: DateModuleOptions) => DateModule['make'];
/**
 * Configuration options for the date module (`config.$date`).
 */
export interface DateModuleOptions {
    /**
     * The date adapter — `nativeDateAdapter` (from `@vueform/core`), a date
     * library adapter (`@vueform/date-dayjs`, `@vueform/date-fns`,
     * `@vueform/date-luxon`), or a custom one. Required: `make` throws when
     * unset, so unused adapters are never bundled.
     */
    adapter?: DateAdapter;
}

import type { ModelNode, ModelStore, SchemaIndex } from '../model';
import type { ExpressionableKeys, ExpressionsProp, LanguagesProp } from '../../types';
import type { getComponentDef } from '../../utils';
import type { MaybeRef, Ref } from 'vue';
import { type VueformInstance, type VueformConfig } from '../../helpers';
/**
 * Per-node expression-tracking state, attached to `ModelNode.expression` while
 * the node has tracked templates.
 */
export type ExpressionNodeState = {
    tracking: Ref<boolean>;
    untrackOn: string[];
    sources: [string, string][];
    track: () => void;
    untrack: () => void;
    stopLoad?: () => void;
};
/**
 * The per-index expression tracker, attached to `SchemaIndex.expressionTracker`
 * once tracking is activated.
 */
export type ExpressionTracker = {
    init: (node: ModelNode, el$: () => any, initOptions?: ExpressionInitOptions) => void;
    release: (node: ModelNode) => void;
};
/**
 * The expression module instance, providing expression resolution and path
 * extraction.
 */
export interface ExpressionModule {
    /**
     * Whether the expression module is registered and enabled. `true` for the
     * built-in path adapter and for plugin engines (e.g. expr-eval).
     */
    installed: MaybeRef<boolean>;
    /**
     * Resolves an expression string against form data, returning the computed
     * string result. Returns `undefined` when the input expression is
     * `undefined`.
     *
     * @param exp The expression string (e.g. `'{field} > 5'`).
     * @param data The form data object to evaluate against.
     * @param context$ The element context for path/dataPath resolution and SELF.
     */
    resolve: {
        (exp: string, data?: Record<string, any>, context$?: any): string;
        (exp: undefined, data?: Record<string, any>, context$?: any): undefined;
        (exp: string | undefined, data?: Record<string, any>, context$?: any): string | undefined;
    };
    /**
     * Extracts the element paths referenced inside an expression chain string.
     *
     * @param expressionChain The raw expression string to scan.
     * @param path The base element path for resolving relative references.
     */
    usedPaths: (expressionChain: string, path?: string) => string[];
    /**
     * Warns (dev-only, once per app) that an expression engine is required. No-op
     * when the expression module is registered and enabled (built-in path adapter
     * or a plugin engine).
     */
    warn: () => void;
    /**
     * Per-node `default`-value expression tracking over a model's schema index:
     * activation, node init / re-init / release, the mounted tracking facade
     * (`isTracking` / `track` / `untrack`), and user-event notifications.
     * Context-free — safe to call anywhere, including headless engines. The inert
     * surface returns a no-op tracking whose `activate` reports `false`.
     *
     * @param index The schema index the tracking operates on. May be `undefined`
     *   (standalone elements without a form) — index-dependent methods no-op.
     */
    makeExpressionTracking: (index?: SchemaIndex) => ExpressionTracking;
}
/**
 * Configuration for `makeExpressionTracking(index).activate()`.
 */
export type ExpressionTrackingOptions = {
    /**
     * The model store resolved values are written through.
     */
    store: ModelStore;
    /**
     * The (possibly partial) Vueform configuration.
     */
    config: VueformConfig;
    /**
     * Resolves the languages used for translatable templates (one tracked
     * template per language). A getter so mounted hosts can hand over their
     * reactive `languages` without eager evaluation.
     */
    languages?: () => LanguagesProp | undefined;
    /**
     * Resolves the constants merged under the model in expression resolution data
     * (instance-level `consts` headlessly, the form's resolved `consts` prop when
     * mounted). Callers omit names already registered in
     * `config.$expression.consts`.
     */
    consts?: () => Record<string, any> | undefined;
    /**
     * Resolves the host-level expression allow-list (the form's `expressions`
     * prop), consulted between the node's own `expressions` prop and the config
     * trigger list.
     */
    expressions?: () => ExpressionsProp | undefined;
};
/**
 * Options for re-initializing a node's expression tracking after a schema
 * rebuild.
 */
export type ExpressionInitOptions = {
    /**
     * Whether tracking should start immediately (writing the resolved value).
     * `false` registers the tracker in the untracked state, preserving a user's
     * earlier untrack across schema rebuilds. Defaults to `true`.
     */
    resume?: boolean;
    /**
     * Template sources from the node's previous tracker, used when the current
     * store value is already resolved (no longer a template) and the node's
     * `default` prop offers none — e.g. model-argument templates surviving a
     * schema rebuild.
     */
    prevSources?: [string, string][];
};
/**
 * The tracking surface returned by `makeExpressionTracking(index)`, operating
 * on one schema index.
 */
export interface ExpressionTracking {
    /**
     * Whether a component instance's element can be expression-tracked: tracking
     * is active for the schema index and the component definition opted in via
     * `defineOptions({ expressionable: true })`.
     *
     * @param instance The component instance hosting the element.
     */
    trackable: (instance: Parameters<typeof getComponentDef>[0]) => boolean;
    /**
     * Activates tracking for the schema index unless it's already active (adopted
     * `useModel` instances arrive with the activation their engine created).
     * Returns whether tracking is active — `false` when the expression module is
     * not installed or expressions are disabled.
     *
     * @param options The tracking configuration.
     */
    activate: (options: ExpressionTrackingOptions) => boolean;
    /**
     * Wires expression tracking for a leaf node (idempotent — already tracked
     * nodes are left untouched). No-op when tracking isn't active for the index.
     * Created effects are owned by the caller's active scope.
     *
     * @param node The index node to track.
     * @param el$ Lazily resolves the element context expressions bind to.
     * @param initOptions Rebuild re-initialization options.
     */
    init: (node: ModelNode, el$: () => any, initOptions?: ExpressionInitOptions) => void;
    /**
     * Re-initializes a node's tracking after a schema rebuild changed its facts:
     * releases the current tracker and inits against the new facts, preserving a
     * user's earlier untrack and carrying template sources the store no longer
     * holds (already resolved). Created effects are owned by the caller's active
     * scope.
     *
     * @param node The index node to re-track.
     * @param el$ Lazily resolves the element context expressions bind to.
     */
    reinit: (node: ModelNode, el$: () => any) => void;
    /**
     * Stops tracking a node and clears its state (used when mounted-created nodes
     * are removed from the index).
     *
     * @param node The index node to release.
     */
    release: (node: ModelNode) => void;
    /**
     * Whether the node's expression is currently tracked and auto-updating the
     * value. `false` for untracked and unknown nodes.
     *
     * @param node The index node to check.
     */
    isTracking: (node: ModelNode | undefined) => boolean;
    /**
     * Resumes a node's tracking after an untrack, immediately re-writing the
     * resolved value. No-op for nodes without a tracker.
     *
     * @param node The index node to track.
     */
    track: (node: ModelNode | undefined) => void;
    /**
     * Stops a node's tracking, leaving the current value in place. No-op for
     * nodes without a tracker.
     *
     * @param node The index node to untrack.
     */
    untrack: (node: ModelNode | undefined) => void;
    /**
     * Notifies a node's tracker about a user-driven event (`input` from real user
     * interaction, `load` from data loading), untracking when the node's
     * `untrackOn` includes it.
     *
     * @param node The index node the event happened on.
     * @param event The event kind.
     */
    notify: (node: ModelNode | undefined, event: 'input' | 'load') => void;
    /**
     * Notifies the trackers of every node whose data path is covered by the given
     * data about a user edit — the headless counterpart of per-element `input`
     * events, backing the model instance's `input()` method.
     *
     * @param data The partial model data that was written.
     */
    notifyInputData: (data: Record<string, any>) => void;
}
/**
 * The low-level expression engine produced by an `ExpressionAdapter`. Deals
 * with single expressions only — the `{…}` template-chain format, `undefined`
 * passthrough, result normalization, and warning handling are owned by
 * `createExpression` and never reach the engine.
 */
export interface ExpressionEngine {
    /**
     * Evaluates a single expression (the inner content of one `{…}` template)
     * against form data and returns the stringified result. Returns `undefined`
     * when the expression cannot be parsed. Throws when evaluation fails (e.g.
     * transient forward references, self-referencing expressions).
     *
     * @param expression The single expression to evaluate.
     * @param data The form data object to evaluate against.
     * @param context$ The element context for path/dataPath resolution and SELF.
     */
    evaluate: (expression: string, data?: Record<string, any>, context$?: any) => string | undefined;
    /**
     * Extracts the element paths referenced by a single expression.
     *
     * @param expression The single expression to scan.
     * @param path The base element path for resolving relative references.
     */
    variables: (expression: string, path?: string) => string[];
}
/**
 * A factory that produces the low-level `ExpressionEngine` from the module
 * options and the owning Vueform instance (adapter functions resolve module
 * doorways like date and locale against it). `createExpression` wraps the
 * engine with everything engine-independent: the `{…}` chain format, escapes,
 * result normalization, the transient-warning queue, `installed`, and `warn`.
 */
export type ExpressionAdapter = (options: ExpressionModuleOptions, vueform: VueformInstance) => ExpressionEngine;
/**
 * Configuration options for the expression module (`config.$expression`).
 */
export interface ExpressionModuleOptions {
    /**
     * Whether the expression system is enabled. When `false`, `createExpression`
     * returns the inert passthrough surface (`installed: false`) even when an
     * adapter is configured.
     */
    enabled?: boolean;
    /**
     * Prop keys that allow expression resolution. When set to an array, only
     * listed keys are resolved. Defaults to all expressionable keys.
     */
    trigger?: ExpressionableKeys[];
    /**
     * Whether to log expression parse/evaluation warnings.
     */
    debug?: boolean;
    /**
     * Custom expression functions keyed by name.
     */
    functions?: Record<string, Function>;
    /**
     * Custom expression constants keyed by name.
     */
    consts?: Record<string, any>;
    /**
     * The expression engine factory (e.g. `exprEvalAdapter`). Defaults to
     * `pathExpressionAdapter`, which resolves simple `{path}` interpolation
     * (`{name}`, `{user.name}`, `{list.0.name}`). Operators, function calls, and
     * other syntax require a plugin adapter.
     */
    adapter?: ExpressionAdapter;
}

//// modules/http/error.d.ts
import type { HttpErrorReason, HttpRequestConfig, HttpResponse } from './types';
/**
 * Error class for HTTP failures, carrying the request config, response data,
 * status, and error reason.
 */
export declare class HttpError extends Error {
    /**
     * HTTP status code from the response, if available.
     */
    status?: number;
    /**
     * Parsed response body data, if available.
     */
    data?: any;
    /**
     * The request config that triggered the error.
     */
    config: HttpRequestConfig;
    /**
     * The category of failure (e.g. `'timeout'`, `'network'`, `'http'`).
     */
    reason: HttpErrorReason;
    /**
     * The full HTTP response object, if the server responded.
     */
    response?: HttpResponse;
    /**
     * @param message The error message.
     * @param config The request config that triggered the error.
     * @param reason The category of failure.
     * @param response The full HTTP response, if the server responded.
     */
    constructor(message: string, config: HttpRequestConfig, reason?: HttpErrorReason, response?: HttpResponse);
}

/**
 * The Fetch-backed adapter: no dependencies, uses the global `fetch`. Not wired
 * in by default — presets that want it configure it explicitly via
 * `$http.adapter`, so consumers who bring their own adapter (axios, ky, a
 * custom one) never bundle this implementation.
 */
export declare const fetchHttpAdapter: HttpAdapter;

import type { VueformInstance } from '../../helpers';
import type { HttpModule } from './types';
/**
 * Returns the resolved instance's http module, or the inert `noopHttp` surface
 * (every request rejects with a descriptive error) when the `http` module is
 * not registered. Resolves the explicit `vueform` (a `createVueform()` instance
 * or config) when given, otherwise the config injected by the calling
 * component's app.
 */
export declare function getHttpModule(vueform?: VueformInstance): HttpModule;
