 * Whether an http module is registered — `false` means `getHttpModule` serves
 * the inert `noopHttp` surface, whose requests reject.
 */
export declare function hasHttpModule(vueform?: VueformInstance): boolean;

//// modules/http/noop.d.ts
import type { HttpModule } from './types';
/**
 * The inert http surface served when the `http` module is not registered.
 * Acquiring it (`useHttp()`, `getHttpModule()`, a component's `$http`) never
 * throws — every request made through it rejects with a descriptive error, so
 * forms and elements that never hit the network work without the module.
 */
export declare const noopHttp: HttpModule;

//// modules/http/resolveUrl.d.ts
/**
 * Joins a request URL with the configured `baseURL` exactly the way the fetch
 * adapter does. The origin gate in `createHttp.request` judges this same value,
 * so the URL that is policy-checked and the URL that is actually requested can
 * never drift apart — both call sites share this one definition.
 *
 * A URL is absolute (and skips the join) only when it starts with `http://` or
 * `https://`; everything else — including scheme-relative `//host` forms, which
 * the join collapses into the base path — is appended to the base. Without a
 * `baseURL` the URL passes through untouched.
 *
 * @param url The request URL from the config.
 * @param baseURL The configured base URL, if any.
 */
export declare function resolveRequestUrl(url: string, baseURL?: string): string;

//// modules/http/types.d.ts
/**
 * Expected response body type.
 */
type ResponseType = 'json' | 'text' | 'blob' | 'arrayBuffer';
/**
 * An HTTP method that accepts a URL, optional request body, and optional config
 * overrides.
 */
type HttpMethodWithData = <T = any>(url: string, data?: any, c?: Partial<HttpRequestConfig>) => Promise<HttpResponse<T>>;
/**
 * An HTTP method that accepts a URL and optional config overrides (no body).
 */
type HttpMethodWithoutData = <T = any>(url: string, c?: Partial<HttpRequestConfig>) => Promise<HttpResponse<T>>;
/**
 * An interceptor that can inspect or modify the request config before the
 * request is sent. May be async.
 */
export type RequestInterceptor = (config: HttpRequestConfig) => HttpRequestConfig | Promise<HttpRequestConfig>;
/**
 * An interceptor that can inspect or modify the response before it is returned
 * to the caller. May be async.
 */
export type ResponseInterceptor = (response: HttpResponse) => HttpResponse | Promise<HttpResponse>;
/**
 * HTTP request method.
 */
export type RequestMethod = ('GET' | 'HEAD' | 'OPTIONS' | 'TRACE' | 'PUT' | 'DELETE' | 'POST' | 'PATCH' | 'CONNECT') | (string & {});
/**
 * Content encoding type for the request body.
 */
export type RequestType = 'json' | 'form' | 'multipart' | 'text' | 'urlencoded';
/**
 * The reason category for an HTTP error.
 */
export type HttpErrorReason = 'timeout' | 'network' | 'abort' | 'http' | 'blocked' | 'ssr' | 'unknown';
/**
 * Global configuration options for the http module (`config.$http`).
 */
export interface HttpModuleOptions {
    /**
     * Default HTTP method when none is specified per request.
     */
    defaultMethod?: RequestMethod;
    /**
     * Default headers sent with every request.
     */
    headers?: Record<string, string>;
    /**
     * Default request timeout in milliseconds.
     */
    timeout?: number;
    /**
     * Base URL prepended to relative request URLs.
     */
    baseURL?: string;
    /**
     * Default body encoding type for requests.
     */
    requestType?: RequestType;
    /**
     * Default expected response body type.
     */
    responseType?: ResponseType;
    /**
     * Whether to include credentials (cookies) in cross-origin requests.
     */
    withCredentials?: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether to automatically convert `File`/`Blob` values to base64 in JSON
     * request bodies.
     */
    base64?: boolean;
    /**
     * App-wide request interceptors, run on every request — submissions,
     * autosave, and instance calls alike (after any instance-registered ones).
     */
    onRequest?: RequestInterceptor[];
    /**
     * App-wide response interceptors, run on every response (before any
     * instance-registered ones).
     */
    onResponse?: ResponseInterceptor[];
    /**
     * The HTTP adapter — `fetchHttpAdapter` (from `@vueform/core`) or a custom
     * one. Required: `request` throws when unset, so an unused Fetch
     * implementation is never bundled.
     */
    adapter?: HttpAdapter;
}
/**
 * Per-request configuration passed to the HTTP adapter.
 */
export interface HttpRequestConfig {
    /**
     * The request URL (absolute or relative to `baseURL`).
     */
    url: string;
    /**
     * HTTP method for this request.
     */
    method?: RequestMethod;
    /**
     * Request body data.
     */
    data?: any;
    /**
     * URL query parameters appended to the request URL.
     */
    params?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined | null>;
    /**
     * Additional headers for this request (merged with defaults).
     */
    headers?: Record<string, string>;
    /**
     * Timeout in milliseconds for this request.
     */
    timeout?: number;
    /**
     * An `AbortSignal` to cancel the request.
     */
    signal?: AbortSignal;
    /**
     * Base URL prepended to the request URL when it is relative.
     */
    baseURL?: string;
    /**
     * Body encoding type for this request.
     */
    requestType?: RequestType;
    /**
     * Expected response body type for this request.
     */
    responseType?: ResponseType;
    /**
     * Whether to include credentials (cookies) in cross-origin requests.
     */
    withCredentials?: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether to convert `File`/`Blob` values to base64 in the request body.
     */
    base64?: boolean;
}
/**
 * Normalized HTTP response returned by all adapters.
 */
export interface HttpResponse<T = any> {
    /**
     * The parsed response body.
     */
    data: T;
    /**
     * HTTP status code.
     */
    status: number;
    /**
     * HTTP status text (e.g. `"OK"`).
     */
    statusText: string;
    /**
     * Response headers as a flat key-value map.
     */
    headers: Record<string, string>;
    /**
     * The request config that produced this response.
     */
    config: HttpRequestConfig;
}
/**
 * An HTTP adapter function that performs the actual network request.
 */
export type HttpAdapter = <T = any>(config: HttpRequestConfig) => Promise<HttpResponse<T>>;
/**
 * The client surface shared by the http module and its instances: the full
 * request method plus the verb shorthands.
 */
export interface HttpClient {
    /**
     * Sends an HTTP request using the configured adapter, applying interceptors
     * and default settings.
     *
     * @param reqConfig The request configuration.
     */
    request: <T = any>(reqConfig: HttpRequestConfig) => Promise<HttpResponse<T>>;
    /**
     * Sends a GET request.
     */
    get: HttpMethodWithoutData;
    /**
     * Sends a POST request.
     */
    post: HttpMethodWithData;
    /**
     * Sends a PUT request.
     */
    put: HttpMethodWithData;
    /**
     * Sends a PATCH request.
     */
    patch: HttpMethodWithData;
    /**
     * Sends a DELETE request.
     */
    delete: HttpMethodWithoutData;
}
/**
 * The http module: the client surface with the app's defaults and
 * config-declared interceptors, plus the factory producing consumer instances.
 */
export interface HttpModule extends HttpClient {
    /**
     * Creates an instance over this module — what `useHttp()` returns.
     */
    make: () => HttpInstance;
}
/**
 * A consumer instance over the shared http module, produced by `make()` and
 * returned by `useHttp()`. Requests made through it run the instance's own
 * interceptors on top of the config-declared ones; interceptors registered here
 * affect only this instance's calls and are released with it. App-wide
 * interceptors are config-declared (`$http.onRequest` / `onResponse`).
 */
export interface HttpInstance extends HttpClient {
    /**
     * Registers a request interceptor for this instance, run on its requests
     * before the config-declared interceptors.
     *
     * @param fn The interceptor function.
     */
    onRequest: (fn: RequestInterceptor) => void;
    /**
     * Registers a response interceptor for this instance, run on responses to its
     * requests after the config-declared interceptors.
     *
     * @param fn The interceptor function.
     */
    onResponse: (fn: ResponseInterceptor) => void;
}
export {};

//// modules/locale/noop.d.ts
import type { LocaleModule } from './types';
/**
 * The inert locale surface used when the `locale` module is not registered —
 * behaves as if localization weren't there: translation tags resolve to their
 * raw tag string, locale maps fall back to their first entry, and locale
 * switching warns in dev.
 */
export declare const noopLocale: LocaleModule;

//// modules/locale/types.d.ts
import { type MaybeRef, type WritableComputedRef } from 'vue';
import type { LocalesProp } from '../../types';
import type { LocaleTag } from './createLocale';
/**
 * The locale module instance providing translation, localization, and locale
 * switching.
 */
export interface LocaleModule {
    /**
     * The currently active locale key (readable and writable).
     */
    locale: WritableComputedRef<string, string>;
    /**
     * Merged translation tags from the active locale and the fallback locale.
     */
    tags: {
        [x: string]: string | (() => string);
    };
    /**
     * The registered locale definitions keyed by locale name.
     */
    locales: LocalesProp;
    /**
     * The fallback locale key used when a translation is missing from the active
     * locale.
     */
    fallbackLocale: string | (string & {});
    /**
     * Translates a locale tag key, substituting optional parameters.
     *
     * @param tag The translation tag key.
     * @param params Optional parameter values to interpolate.
     */
    t: (tag: LocaleTag, params?: Record<string, string | number>) => string;
    /**
     * Replaces parameter placeholders in a message string with the corresponding
     * parameter values. Placeholders are identified by the `localeParamPattern`
     * config option (defaults to `{param}`).
     *
     * @param msg The message template containing placeholders.
     * @param params Key-value pairs to substitute.
     */
    replaceParams: (msg: string, params?: Record<string, string | number>) => string;
    /**
     * Sets the active locale by key.
     *
     * @param locale The locale key to switch to.
     */
    setLocale: (locale: string) => void;
    /**
     * Sets the active locale by key.
     *
     * @param locale The locale key to switch to.
     */
    set: (locale: string) => void;
    /**
     * Resolves a localizable value — returns the string for the active locale
     * when given a locale-keyed object, or the string itself when given a plain
     * string.
     *
     * @param msg A plain string or a `{ locale: translation }` map.
     */
    localize: (msg?: string | Record<string, string>) => string;
    /**
     * Localizes every value in a `{ value: label }` map, returning a flat
     * `Record<string, string>` with resolved labels.
     *
     * @param obj An object whose values are plain strings or locale-keyed maps.
     */
    localizeObject: (obj: Record<string, string | Record<string, string>>) => Record<string, string>;
}
/**
 * A factory that produces a `LocaleModule` instance.
 */
export type LocaleAdapter = (options: LocaleModuleOptions) => LocaleModule;
/**
 * Configuration options for the locale module (`config.$locale`).
 */
export interface LocaleModuleOptions {
    /**
     * Registered locale definitions keyed by locale name.
     */
    locales?: LocalesProp;
    /**
     * Fallback locale key used when a translation is missing.
     */
    fallbackLocale?: string;
    /**
     * Active locale key (or a ref to one).
     */
    locale?: MaybeRef<string>;
    /**
     * Pattern used to interpolate `{param}` placeholders in messages.
     */
    localeParamPattern?: RegExp;
    /**
     * Custom locale implementation replacing the built-in translator.
     */
    adapter?: LocaleAdapter;
}

//// modules/model/createModel.d.ts
import { type ComputedRef, type Ref } from 'vue';
import type { ModelModule, ModelNode, RootModel } from './types';
import { type VueformInstance } from '../../helpers';
import { type ElementName } from '../../types';
/**
 * Configuration options for `makeRootModel`.
 */
type MakeRootModelOptions = {
    /**
     * The reactive ref bound to the form's `v-model`, used as the initial source
     * of truth for the root model. When it holds a `useModel` instance, its store
     * is adopted directly (shared data, no clone or v-model sync).
     */
    modelValue: Ref<any>;
    /**
     * Whether the component has an active `v-model` binding (raw prop detection,
     * supplied by the component adapter). Adopted stores override it to `false`
     * internally — the store is the single source of truth, so no v-model
     * emission happens.
     */
    hasVModel: Ref<boolean>;
    /**
     * The form's component context, recorded on adopted stores (backing
     * `instance.submit()`) and passed to `change` events. Opaque to the module.
     */
    context$: any;
    /**
     * Whether any callback is registered for the given event. When provided, the
     * notify watcher skips the model snapshot (a deep clone of the whole model)
     * on flushes where neither a `v-model` nor a `change` listener would consume
     * it. When omitted, a snapshot is taken on every flush.
     */
    hasListeners?: (e: 'change') => boolean;
    /**
     * Applies an inbound external `modelValue` change to the root model (e.g. the
     * form context's `update`).
     *
     * @param data The new (cloned) model value from outside.
     */
    applyInbound: (data: any) => void;
    /**
     * Event emitter for firing model change events during synchronization: the
     * `change` event on value changes and `update:modelValue` for v-model sync.
     */
    fire: {
        (e: 'change', newValue: any, oldValue: any, context$: any): any;
        (e: 'update:modelValue', value: any): any;
    };
};
/**
 * Configuration options for `makeChildModel`.
 */
type MakeChildModelOptions = {
    /**
     * The parent model surface the element reads from and writes to — typed
     * structurally so the module never learns component container semantics.
     */
    parent: {
        /**
         * The parent's model object holding this element's slice.
         */
        model: Ref<any>;
        /**
         * Writes a value at an absolute data path within the root model.
         *
         * @param path The absolute dot-notation data path.
         * @param value The value to set.
         */
        update: (path: string, value: any) => void;
        /**
         * Subscribes to changes at an absolute data path (and its descendants),
         * returning an unsubscribe function.
         *
         * @param path The absolute dot-notation data path.
         * @param cb The callback invoked when the path's subtree changes.
         */
        subscribe: (path: string, cb: () => void) => () => void;
    };
    /**
     * The element's name, used as the key into the parent's model.
     */
    name: Ref<ElementName>;
    /**
     * The element's absolute data path within the root model, used to subscribe
     * to changes of its slice (and its descendants).
     */
    dataPath: Ref<string>;
    /**
     * The external `v-model` ref bound by the parent, if any.
     */
    modelValue?: Ref<any>;
    /**
     * Whether the element is currently available (visible). Unavailable elements
     * skip outbound model synchronization.
     */
    available?: Ref<boolean>;
    /**
     * Whether the element's data is flattened into the parent rather than nested
     * under its own `name` key. Flat containers project a scoped model from their
     * own children's keys and subscribe to those keys individually instead of
     * their own data path (which equals the parent's).
     */
    flat: Ref<boolean>;
    /**
     * The element's registered child contexts. Required for flat containers,
     * whose scoped model is built from these children's keys within the parent's
     * model. Opaque to the module beyond `isFlatContainer` / `name` / `model`.
     */
    children?: Ref<any[]>;
    /**
     * Whether the component has an active `v-model` binding (raw prop detection,
     * supplied by the component adapter).
     */
    hasVModel: Ref<boolean>;
    /**
     * The element's component context passed to `change` events. Opaque to the
     * module.
     */
    context$: any;
    /**
     * Event emitter for firing model change events during synchronization: the
     * `change` event on value changes and `update:modelValue` for v-model sync.
     */
    fire: {
        (e: 'change', newValue: any, oldValue: any, context$: any): any;
        (e: 'update:modelValue', value: any): any;
    };
    /**
     * Writes the given value back to the parent's model for this element
     * (typically the element's own `update` method), also used to apply inbound
     * `v-model` changes.
     *
     * @param data The new value to set.
     */
    update: (data: any) => void;
    /**
     * Whether any callback is registered for the given event. When provided and
     * neither a `v-model` nor a `change` listener would consume the notification,
     * the notify watcher skips firing events and skips the model snapshot (a deep
     * clone of the element's slice) on flushes where the value did not change.
     * When omitted, the full notify path runs on every flush.
     */
    hasListeners?: (e: 'change') => boolean;
};
/**
 * Creates the model module instance from the app config. The module is a
 * stateless factory: `make` builds standalone form models from schemas using
 * the component definitions registered in the config, while per-form state
 * lives in the produced instances.
 *
 * The returned instances own their data and expose the familiar data API
 * (`update` / `load` / `clear` / `reset` / `clean`, `dirty` / `empty`,
 * path-based `get` / `set`, `toJSON` / `toFormData`). Passing one to a form's
 * `v-model` (or `useForm`) makes the form adopt it — the same store is shared
 * without cloning, and `submit()` becomes available.
 *
 * ```ts
 * const model$ = createModel(config).make(schema, { name: 'John' })
 *
 * model$.model.name // 'John'
 * model$.set('email', 'john@example.com')
 * model$.dirty // true
 * ```
 *
 * @param vueform The owning instance, whose config the model shape depends on
 *   via the registered component definitions.
 */
export declare function createModel(vueform: VueformInstance): ModelModule;
/**
 * Creates the root-level reactive model for a form, providing model sync,
 * registration, and lifecycle methods.
 *
 * Always backed by a model store and schema index: when `modelValue` holds a
 * `useModel` instance the form adopts its store and index (the store stays the
 * single source of truth — no v-model emission or inbound watcher), otherwise a
 * store is created internally from the plain `modelValue` and kept in sync with
 * it, with an empty index filled by mounted registration.
 *
 * @param options Root model configuration object.
 */
export declare function makeRootModel(options: MakeRootModelOptions): RootModel;
/**
 * Creates the reactive model for a child element by reading from its parent
 * container's model and keeping it in sync with the element's `v-model`,
 * mirroring the lifecycle interface of `makeRootModel`.
 *
 * @param options Child model configuration object.
 */
export declare function makeChildModel(options: MakeChildModelOptions): {
    model: ComputedRef<any>;
    lastModel: Ref<any, any>;
    initialModel: Ref<any, any>;
    init: () => void;
    destroy: () => void;
};
/**
 * Creates an index node for a mounted element the schema walk didn't produce
 * (template-driven elements, or list rows added beyond the initial count). Only
 * identity facts are known up front — the claimed component context carries the
 * live state.
 *
 * @param facts The element's path and data path.
 */
export declare function makeMountedNode(facts: {
    path: string;
    dataPath?: string;
}): ModelNode;
export {};

//// modules/model/modelStore.d.ts
import type { ModelInstance, ModelStore } from './types';
/**
 * Configuration options for `makeModelStore`.
 */
type ModelStoreOptions = {
    /**
     * The initial model object the store takes ownership of. Not cloned — the
     * caller is responsible for passing an owned object.
     */
    model?: Record<string, any>;
    /**
     * The null-value tree matching the model's shape, used by `clear()` and the
     * `empty` computed. Dynamic containers (lists, dynamic matrices) appear as
     * arrays holding their initial rows' null values.
     */
    nullModel?: Record<string, any>;
};
export type ModelStoreEvents = 'change' | 'load' | 'clear' | 'reset';
/**
 * Creates a component-independent model store: the single owner of a form model
 * object with path-based reads/writes, subscriber-based change dispatching, and
 * data manipulation methods (`update` / `load` / `clear` / `reset` / `clean`)
 * plus `dirty` / `empty` state.
 *
 * Both `useModel` (standalone data ownership) and VfForm's internal root model
 * (`useData`) are built on top of it. When a `useModel` instance is passed to a
 * form, the form adopts this store directly, so the data is shared without
 * cloning.
 *
 * @param options Model store configuration object.
 */
export declare function makeModelStore(options?: ModelStoreOptions): {
    model: import("vue").Ref<Record<string, any>, Record<string, any>>;
    initialModel: import("vue").Ref<Record<string, any>, Record<string, any>>;
    nullModel: Record<string, any> | undefined;
    adopted: import("vue").Ref<boolean, boolean>;
    adoptingContext: import("vue").Ref<any, any>;
    notifyTrigger: import("vue").Ref<number, number>;
    dirty: import("vue").ComputedRef<boolean>;
    empty: import("vue").ComputedRef<boolean>;
    subscribe: (dataPath: string, cb: () => void) => () => void;
    dispatch: (dataPath: string) => void;
    onWrite: (cb: (dataPath: string) => void) => () => void;
    get: (dataPath?: string) => any;
    set: (dataPath: string, value: any) => void;
    register: (dataPath: string, initialModel: any) => void;
    unregister: (dataPath: string) => void;
    update: (data: any) => void;
    load: (data: any) => void;
    clear: () => void;
    reset: () => void;
    clean: () => void;
    toJSON: () => string;
    toFormData: () => FormData;
    on: (event: ModelStoreEvents, cb: (...args: any[]) => void) => () => void;
    fire: (event: ModelStoreEvents, ...args: any[]) => void;
    consumeValueChanged: () => boolean;
    adopt: (context$: any) => void;
    release: () => void;
    submit: () => Promise<any>;
    destroy: () => void;
};
/**
 * Binds a model instance to its backing store. Used as both the instance brand
 * (`hasModelStore`) and the store accessor (`getModelStore`).
 *
 * @param instance The model instance to brand.
 * @param store The store to bind.
 */
export declare function setModelStore(instance: object, store: ModelStore): void;
/**
 * Returns the underlying model store of a `useModel` instance.
 *
 * Module-internal — consumed by `makeRootModel` for form adoption, never
 * exposed outside the module.
 *
 * @param instance The model instance to unwrap.
 */
export declare function getModelStore(instance: ModelInstance<any>): ModelStore;
/**
 * Whether a value is a `useModel` instance. VfForm checks `modelValue` with it
 * to adopt the instance's store directly instead of cloning the data.
 *
 * @param value The value to check.
 */
export declare function hasModelStore(value: any): value is ModelInstance;
export {};

import type { VueformInstance } from '../../helpers';
import type { ModelModule } from './types';
/**
 * Returns the resolved instance's model module. Throws when the module is not
 * registered. Resolves the explicit `vueform` (a `createVueform()` instance or
 * config) when given, otherwise the config injected by the calling component's
 * app.
 */
export declare function getModelModule(vueform?: VueformInstance): ModelModule;

//// modules/model/types.d.ts
import type { ConditionalProp } from '../conditions';
import type { ExpressionNodeState, ExpressionTracker } from '../expression';
import type { Issue, RulesProp, TRulesProp } from '../validation';
import type { ArraySchema, DeepPartial, ExactValidatedSchema, FormSchema, ModelByPath, ObjectSchema, Paths, SchemaToModel, StandardSchemaV1, StatefulElement } from '../../types';
import type { makeChildModel, makeMountedNode, makeRootModel } from './createModel';
import type { hasModelStore, makeModelStore, ModelStoreEvents } from './modelStore';
import type { Ref } from 'vue';
/**
 * The model module instance: a stateless factory capturing the app config.
 * `make` builds a standalone form model from a schema — per-form state lives in
 * the returned `ModelInstance`, not the module. The model kit (root / child
 * model creation, the data store, mounted-node creation, and instance branding)
 * is config-free and also available on the fallback surface when the module is
 * not registered.
 */
export interface ModelModule {
    /**
     * Creates the root-level reactive model for a form, providing model sync,
     * registration, and lifecycle methods.
     */
    makeRootModel: typeof makeRootModel;
    /**
     * Creates the reactive model for a child element by reading from its parent
     * container's model, mirroring the lifecycle interface of `makeRootModel`.
     */
    makeChildModel: typeof makeChildModel;
    /**
     * Creates a standalone reactive model store.
     */
    makeModelStore: typeof makeModelStore;
    /**
     * Creates an index node for a mounted element the schema walk didn't produce.
     */
    makeMountedNode: typeof makeMountedNode;
    /**
     * Whether a value carries a model store (a `useModel` instance).
     */
    hasModelStore: typeof hasModelStore;
    /**
     * Creates a standalone form model from a schema: the full data shape is built
     * up front from the elements' model metadata (defaults, null values,
     * translatable expansion), without mounting any components.
     *
     * @param schema The form schema describing the model's shape. When a
     *   ref/computed is passed (e.g. from `defineComputedSchema`), the instance
     *   follows schema changes: the index is reconciled in place, added elements
     *   seed their defaults, removed elements drop their data, and the headless
     *   engines re-wire — existing values and expression untrack state survive.
     * @param model Initial (partial) data cloned over the schema defaults. A Vue
     *   ref is rejected (dev warn, seed ignored) — pass a plain or reactive
     *   object. Later mutations of the seed are ignored.
     * @param validationSchema A Standard Schema run by `validate()` against the
     *   whole model; overrides one attached via `defineSchema`.
     */
    make<const S extends (ObjectSchema | ArraySchema) & ExactValidatedSchema<S>>(schema: S | Ref<S>, model?: DeepPartial<SchemaToModel<S>> & Record<string, any>, validationSchema?: StandardSchemaV1): ModelInstance<S>;
    make(schema: FormSchema | Ref<FormSchema>, model?: Record<string, any>, validationSchema?: StandardSchemaV1): ModelInstance;
}
/**
 * Configuration options for the model module (`config.$model`).
 */
export interface ModelModuleOptions {
}
/**
 * A node in the schema index: one data-carrying element (leaf or container)
 * with its resolved model metadata. Nodes are created by the schema walk and
 * later claimable by mounted components.
 */
export type ModelNode = {
    /**
     * The element path (e.g. `address.city`), including flat containers' names.
     */
    path: string;
    /**
     * The data path within the model. Flat containers share their parent's data
     * path (`''` at the root); their children write to the parent's level.
     */
    dataPath: string;
    /**
     * The parent node, if any.
     */
    parent?: ModelNode;
    /**
     * Child nodes by name (containers only). Array containers key their rows by
     * index (`'0'`, `'1'`, …) as built from the initial row count.
     */
    children?: Map<string, ModelNode>;
    /**
     * Whether the node's data lives merged at the parent's level instead of
     * nested under its own key.
     */
    flat: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether the node is an array-like container (e.g. list).
     */
    array: boolean;
    /**
     * The schema entry type (e.g. `text`, `group`).
     */
    type?: string;
    /**
     * The schema-entry props (with `name` applied). Overridable by mounted
     * elements once claimed.
     */
    props: Record<string, any>;
    /**
     * The node's null value (containers: the assembled null tree of their
     * children).
     */
    nullValue: any;
    /**
     * Whether the node's value is expanded into a locale-keyed object.
     */
    translatable: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether the node's data is included in the submit payload.
     */
    submit: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether the node's component opted into `default`-value expression tracking
     * (`defineOptions({ expressionable: true })`). Resolved from the component
     * definition by the walk, or set at claim time for registration-created
     * nodes.
     */
    expressionable?: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether the node was created by mounted registration (as opposed to the
     * schema walk) — such nodes carry element facts (props, translatability)
     * filled in at claim time and are removed again on unregistration.
     */
    mounted?: boolean;
    /**
     * A human-readable name for validation messages, mirroring the mounted
     * `genericName` chain (`displayName` → `label` → `floating` → `floatLabel` →
     * `ifta` → `placeholder` → `name`) for statically resolvable props.
     */
    genericName: string;
    /**
     * Validation rules declared on the schema entry.
     */
    rules?: RulesProp | TRulesProp;
    /**
     * Conditions declared on the schema entry.
     */
    conditions?: ConditionalProp;
    /**
     * Availability resolved by the conditions engine (attached lazily by the
     * model instance; `undefined` means unconditionally available).
     */
    available?: Ref<boolean>;
    /**
     * The mounted component context once claimed (form flip phase).
     */
    el$?: object;
    /**
     * Expression-tracking state attached by the expression module while the node
     * has tracked templates (`init` sets it, `release` clears it).
     */
    expression?: ExpressionNodeState;
};
/**
 * The result of a schema walk: the node tree plus the default model (with
 * `modelValue` / `default` precedence applied) and the matching null-value
 * tree, all derived from the same traversal.
 */
export type SchemaIndex = {
    /**
     * Top-level nodes by name.
     */
    root: Map<string, ModelNode>;
    /**
     * All nodes in the tree, keyed by element path for O(1) lookup.
     */
    nodes: Map<string, ModelNode>;
    /**
     * The complete default model derived from the schema.
     */
    model: Record<string, any>;
    /**
     * The null-value tree matching the model's shape, used for `clear()` and
     * `empty` checks.
     */
    nullModel: Record<string, any>;
    /**
     * Bumped whenever the index's mounted bindings change (a node is claimed or
     * released, or a validation map is attached), so engine aggregates depending
     * on them re-collect.
     */
    version: Ref<number>;
    /**
     * The expression tracker attached by the expression module once tracking is
     * activated for this index (one per index, shared by the headless engine and
     * the mounted form).
     */
    expressionTracker?: ExpressionTracker;
};
/**
 * A standalone model store returned by `makeModelStore`.
 */
export type ModelStore = ReturnType<typeof import('./modelStore').makeModelStore>;
/**
 * The root-level form model returned by `makeRootModel`: the store-backed model
 * refs plus the registration and lifecycle interface owned by the element
 * operating as the form root. `makeChildModel` mirrors the model refs and
 * lifecycle subset of this interface.
 */
export type RootModel = {
    /**
     * The backing model store — the form's own, or the adopted `useModel` store
     * when `modelValue` carries one.
     */
    store: ModelStore;
    /**
     * Whether the model adopted an existing `useModel` store from `modelValue`
     * instead of creating its own.
     */
    adopted: boolean;
    /**
     * The schema index describing every data-carrying element: the adopted
     * instance's index, or an empty one for internally created stores.
     */
    index: SchemaIndex;
    /**
     * The adopted `useModel` instance's element lookup, `undefined` when the
     * store was created internally.
     */
    modelFind: ((path: string) => StatefulElement | undefined) | undefined;
    /**
     * The reactive model object holding all element values.
     */
    model: Ref<Record<string, any>>;
    /**
     * A snapshot of the model taken at init, used for change detection.
     */
    lastModel: Ref<any>;
    /**
     * A snapshot of the model at creation time (re-snapshotted by `clean()`),
     * used for dirty checking and reset.
     */
    initialModel: Ref<Record<string, any>>;
    /**
     * Sets the value at the given data path within the model.
     */
    set: (dataPath: string, value: any) => void;
    /**
     * Registers an element's data path in the model, seeding its initial value.
     */
    register: (dataPath: string, initialModel: any) => void;
    /**
     * Removes an element's data path from the model. No-op once the form is torn
     * down when the store is adopted, so the store's data survives child
     * unregistration.
     */
    unregister: (dataPath: string) => void;
    /**
     * Subscribes a callback to writes at the given data path, returning an
     * unsubscribe function.
     */
    subscribe: (dataPath: string, cb: () => void) => () => void;
    /**
     * Initializes the model: takes the initial snapshots, emits the initial
     * v-model value, and starts inbound watching (own stores only).
     */
    init: () => void;
    /**
     * Tears down the model binding and releases (adopted) or destroys (own) the
     * store.
     */
    destroy: () => void;
};
/**
 * A standalone form model created by `useModel`: owns the data of a schema
 * outside any form, with unwrapped reactive state (`model`, `dirty`, `empty` —
 * no `.value`) and the full data manipulation API. Passing it to a form's
 * `v-model` makes the form adopt it, after which `submit()` and `adopted`
 * reflect the form.
 */
export type ModelInstance<TSchema = FormSchema> = {
    /**
     * The reactive model object holding all element values.
     */
    readonly model: SchemaToModel<TSchema>;
    /**
     * A snapshot of the model at creation time (re-snapshotted by `clean()`),
     * used for dirty checking and reset.
     */
    readonly initialModel: SchemaToModel<TSchema>;
    /**
     * Whether the current model differs from the initial model snapshot.
     */
    readonly dirty: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether every value in the model is empty (blank or equal to its null
     * value).
     */
    readonly empty: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether a form has adopted the model (via `v-model` / `useForm`).
     */
    readonly adopted: boolean;
    /**
     * The schema index: the node tree describing every data-carrying element,
     * built by the schema walk.
     */
    readonly index: SchemaIndex;
    /**
     * The full model data, unavailable elements included (same as `model` —
     * mirrors the mounted `data` semantics).
     */
    readonly data: SchemaToModel<TSchema>;
    /**
     * The submit payload: the model filtered to available, submittable elements
     * (unavailable and `submit: false` elements are excluded).
     */
    readonly payload: DeepPartial<SchemaToModel<TSchema>>;
    /**
     * The form-level Standard Schema run by `validate()`, if any (explicit
     * `validationSchema` option or one attached via `defineSchema`'s second
     * argument). An adopting form picks it up when it has no own.
     */
    readonly validationSchema: StandardSchemaV1 | undefined;
    /**
     * Whether any validated element is currently invalid.
     */
    readonly invalid: boolean;
    /**
     * Aggregated error messages from every validated element.
     */
    readonly errors: string[];
    /**
     * Structured validation issues from every validated element (and the
     * form-level Standard Schema, if any).
     */
    readonly issues: Issue[];
    /**
     * Returns the value at the given data path within the model. With no path,
     * returns the whole model object.
     *
     * @param path The dot-notation data path to read.
     */
    get: {
        (): SchemaToModel<TSchema>;
        <P extends Paths<TSchema> | (string & {})>(path: P): ModelByPath<TSchema, P>;
    };
    /**
     * Sets the value at the given data path within the model.
     *
     * @param path The dot-notation data path to write.
     * @param value The value to assign.
     */
    set: <P extends Paths<TSchema> | (string & {})>(path: P, value: ModelByPath<TSchema, P>) => void;
    /**
     * Updates the model from a (partial) data object: plain objects are
     * deep-merged, arrays and leaves are replaced.
     *
     * @param data The data to merge into the model.
     */
    update: (data: DeepPartial<SchemaToModel<TSchema>>) => void;
    /**
     * Updates the model like `update`, but as a user edit: expression-tracked
     * elements covered by the data stop tracking (per their `untrackOn`) — the
     * headless counterpart of typing into a mounted element.
     *
     * @param data The data to merge into the model.
     */
    input: (data: DeepPartial<SchemaToModel<TSchema>>) => void;
    /**
     * Loads data into the model (same merge semantics as `update`) and fires the
     * `load` event.
     *
     * @param data The data to load.
     */
    load: (data: DeepPartial<SchemaToModel<TSchema>>) => void;
    /**
     * Clears the model to its null values (dynamic container arrays become
     * empty).
     */
    clear: () => void;
    /**
     * Resets the model to the initial model snapshot.
     */
    reset: () => void;
    /**
     * Marks the model as clean by re-snapshotting the initial model from the
     * current model.
     */
    clean: () => void;
    /**
     * Serializes the current model to a JSON string.
     */
    toJSON: () => string;
    /**
     * Serializes the current model to a `FormData` instance.
     */
    toFormData: () => FormData;
    /**
     * Subscribes a listener to a model event, returning an unsubscribe function.
     *
     * @param event The event name.
     * @param cb The listener to register.
     */
    on: (event: ModelStoreEvents, cb: (...args: any[]) => void) => () => void;
    /**
     * Submits the adopting form. Warns and resolves `undefined` when no form has
     * adopted the model.
     */
    submit: () => Promise<any>;
    /**
     * Returns the (virtual) element context at the given element path (e.g.
     * `address.city`, including flat containers' names), or `undefined` when no
     * such element exists.
     *
     * @param path The dot-notation element path to look up.
     */
    find: (path: string) => StatefulElement | undefined;
    /**
     * Validates every available element with rules (per language when
     * translatable), plus the form-level Standard Schema when configured, and
     * resolves with whether everything is valid.
     */
    validate: () => Promise<boolean>;
    /**
     * Exposes this model's compiled validation as a Standard Schema.
     */
    toStandardSchema: () => StandardSchemaV1;
    /**
     * Stops the instance's watchers and reactive effects (engines, change
     * watcher). The data itself stays readable afterwards.
     */
    destroy: () => void;
};
/**
 * Describes how a container element maps its children into the model, as
 * returned by a component's `children` model metadata function.
 */
export type ModelChildren = {
    /**
     * Whether the container's children data lives merged at the parent's level
     * instead of nested under the container's own key (e.g. non-nested groups and
     * grids).
     */
    flat?: boolean;
    /**
     * Whether the container's model is an array (e.g. list rows, dynamic matrix
     * rows). Entries are then keyed by stringified indices (`'0'`, `'1'`, …).
     */
    array?: boolean;
    /**
     * The unified child schema structure: each key is a child name and each value
     * is the child's schema-entry props (including `type`).
     */
    entries: Record<string, Record<string, any>>;
};
/**
 * Model metadata function returning the element's null (empty) value derived
 * from its raw schema-entry props. Implementations must apply their own prop
 * defaults (e.g. checkbox `falseValue ?? false`).
 *
 * @param props The element's raw schema-entry props.
 */
export type ModelMetaNullValue = (props: Record<string, any>) => any;
/**
 * Model metadata function returning a container element's unified child
 * structure derived from its raw schema-entry props. Leaf elements omit it.
 *
 * @param props The element's raw schema-entry props.
 */
export type ModelMetaChildren = (props: Record<string, any>) => ModelChildren | undefined;

//// modules/security/noop.d.ts
import type { VueformConfig } from '../../helpers';
import type { SecurityModule } from './types';
/**
 * The security surface used when the `security` module is not registered. The
 * module family's rule applies: an absent module means the feature is absent —
 * `validation` absent counts everything valid, `security` absent enforces
 * nothing. Two regimes:
 *
 * - **No configured intent**: fully permissive. HTML renders in every area
 *   (unsanitized — there is no engine), any component name resolves, requests
 *   are unrestricted, prop bags and persisted values pass through untouched.
 *   Deliberately omitting the module is the documented way to opt out of the
 *   protections wholesale — URL scheme checks and CSS containment included.
 *   (Prototype-key guards still apply — they are invariants, not policy — and
 *   slot HTML is inserted with the platform's own `innerHTML` semantics, so
 *   `<script>` elements stay inert regardless.)
 * - **Configured intent without the module** (`allowHtml`, `allowComponents`,
 *   `allowOrigins` entries, `banProps`, ciphers — a config that reads like
 *   policy): in development the surface stays permissive so the app remains
 *   workable, and `createVueform()`'s orphan-`$security`-options warning names
 *   the fix at startup. In production the same state **fails closed** instead —
 *   HTML escapes, components don't resolve, requests are blocked, prop bags
 *   come back empty, ciphers throw — and the misconfiguration can never ship
 *   looking enforced while it isn't. (`allowOrigins: ['*']` is not intent to
 *   restrict: permissive behavior is exactly its configured semantics.)
 *
 * Normal operation is identical in both environments; only the misconfiguration
 * state differs.
 *
 * @param config The config of the instance the noop stands in for.
 */
export declare function noopSecurity(config: VueformConfig): SecurityModule;

//// modules/security/types.d.ts
/**
 * The engine behind the security module's _sanitize_ capability — a function
 * taking raw HTML and returning the safe output (e.g. the DOMPurify wrapper).
 * Engine slots are per-capability, never module-wide: a sanitizer knows nothing
 * about the module's other capabilities (like the encryption ciphers), and a
 * future externally-backed capability would get its own slot.
 */
export type SecuritySanitizer = (html: string) => string;
/**
 * An app-provided encryption or decryption function. Receives the value and a
 * purpose tag identifying the call site (e.g. `'autosave:local'`), so one
 * implementation can serve every feature that encrypts — branching per purpose
 * if it ever needs to. May be async (Web Crypto).
 */
export type SecurityCipher = (value: string, purpose: string) => string | Promise<string>;
/**
 * The areas where a schema string may render as HTML: `content` is
 * `VfContent`'s `content` prop, `slots` are string `slots` entries, and `grid`
 * covers grid string cells.
 */
export type SecurityHtmlArea = 'content' | 'grid' | 'slots';
/**
 * Configuration options for the security module (`config.$security`).
 */
export interface SecurityModuleOptions {
    /**
     * The sanitization engine (e.g. the DOMPurify wrapper). Like the ciphers,
     * there is no built-in one, and HTML rendering in `allowHtml` areas always
     * passes through it. Without an engine, HTML renders raw with a dev warning
     * in development and renders **empty** in production — install
     * `@vueform/dompurify`, or consciously opt out of sanitization by registering
     * an identity function (`sanitizer: (html) => html`).
     */
    sanitizer?: SecuritySanitizer;
    /**
     * Encrypts values before features persist them (e.g. local autosave drafts).
     * There is no built-in cipher — bring a scheme whose key lives outside the
     * stored data, such as a session-delivered key held in memory. When omitted,
     * values are stored as-is.
     */
    encrypt?: SecurityCipher;
    /**
     * The inverse of `encrypt`, applied when persisted values are read back. A
     * `decrypt` that throws marks the stored value unreadable — features treat it
     * as absent (e.g. autosave discards the draft).
     */
    decrypt?: SecurityCipher;
    /**
     * The areas where strings may render as **HTML**. Empty by default: plain
     * text strings always render (escaped), and HTML-looking strings in an area
     * not listed here render escaped. HTML in an allowed area always passes
     * through `sanitizeHtml` — the `sanitizer` engine, or its fallback (raw + dev
     * warning in development, empty in production).
     */
    allowHtml?: SecurityHtmlArea[];
    /**
     * The globally registered component names a string may resolve to — in
     * `slots` entries, the `template` prop, the `layout` prop, and the schema
     * `component` key. Empty by default, so no name resolves; a name outside the
     * list is ignored with a dev warning. Built-in `Vf*` names derived from an
     * element's `type` are exempt (they are the element vocabulary itself).
     */
    allowComponents?: string[];
    /**
     * The **cross-origin** destinations HTTP requests may target, as absolute
     * origins (e.g. `'https://api.example.com'`). Unset is equivalent to `[]`:
     * requests to the app's own origin — relative URLs, and absolute URLs
     * spelling out the current origin — always pass, while everything else is
     * rejected before the request is sent unless its origin is listed. `['*']`
     * opts out of the restriction entirely.
     *
     * Two wildcard forms are supported: `'https://*.example.com'` matches any
     * subdomain (at any depth, never the apex host itself), and
     * `'https://example.com:*'` matches that exact host on any port. A wildcard
     * never widens the scheme.
     *
     * Outside a browser nothing is trusted implicitly — no page origin, no
     * `baseURL` — so an absolute URL passes only when its origin is listed. The
     * HTTP stack is client-side anyway: the built-in fetch adapter refuses SSR
     * requests.
     */
    allowOrigins?: string[];
    /**
     * Keys to drop from every schema-reachable prop bag — schema entries
     * themselves (form entries, group children, flat list prototypes, grid cell /
     * matrix column schemas), `parts` bags, and grid cell `attrs` — **in every
     * value form**. String entries match case-insensitively; RegExp entries as
     * written (add the `i` flag yourself, e.g. `/^on/i`). Both are checked
     * against the original key spelling and its camelized form — Vue camelizes
     * spread keys when matching declared component props, so a ban on `onLabel`
     * also catches `on-label`. Slot HTML is not a prop bag: its attributes are
     * the sanitizer's domain (`sanitizeOptions`).
     *
     * Only a minimal set is banned regardless of this option and cannot be
     * relaxed: prototype keys and `innerHTML` / `outerHTML` — the entries that
     * turn a `v-bind` spread into an HTML sink or re-point object prototypes.
     * Everything else is this option's responsibility. **When schemas can come
     * from untrusted sources, configure at least `[/^on/i, 'srcdoc']`** so inline
     * event handlers (`onclick`, …) and iframe HTML never reach the DOM. Because
     * schema entries pass the same filter, listing a prop name disables that
     * **channel** for schemas while template usage keeps working — e.g.
     * `['style']` (beacon / overlay CSS in both its string and object forms),
     * `['id', 'name']` (DOM clobbering), or `['parts', 'slots', 'tokens']` (no
     * schema-driven presentation at all). Dropped entries warn in development.
     */
    banProps?: (string | RegExp)[];
}
/**
 * The security module instance providing HTML sanitization, schema gating,
 * request-origin policy, and app-level encryption for persisted values.
 */
export interface SecurityModule {
    /**
     * Sanitizes an HTML string for an HTML sink. With a `$security.sanitizer`
     * engine, its output. Without one — like an unconfigured cipher, a state the
     * app should resolve — the string passes through raw with a one-time dev
     * warning in development, and comes back **empty** in production
     * (unsanitizable HTML never ships). Register an identity `sanitizer` to
     * consciously opt out. Returns an empty string for non-string input.
     *
     * @param value The HTML string to sanitize.
     */
    sanitizeHtml: (value?: string) => string;
    /**
     * Filters a schema-reachable prop bag (schema entries, `parts` bags, grid
     * cell `attrs`) down to entries safe to bind: the built-in denylist
     * (`innerHTML`/`outerHTML`, prototype keys) plus the entries matching
     * `$security.banProps` (strings or RegExps), dropped in every value form with
     * a dev warning. Returns the same reference when nothing needs stripping.
     * Filtering is a module feature: without the `security` module registered,
     * bags pass through unchanged.
     *
     * @param props The prop bag to filter.
     */
    sanitizeProps: <T extends Record<string, any>>(props: T) => T;
    /**
     * Guards a schema-supplied CSS value fragment before interpolation into
     * `<style>` text: a `{`/`}` could close the scoped rule and inject arbitrary
     * selectors (e.g. attribute-selector exfiltration of typed input values), so
     * brace-bearing values resolve to `undefined` with a dev warning. Numbers
     * stringify; `null`/`undefined` pass through as `undefined`. Consumed by
     * grid/matrix layout CSS and theme token values. Without the module, values
     * pass through unchecked.
     *
     * @param value The candidate CSS value fragment.
     */
    sanitizeCss: (value: string | number | null | undefined) => string | undefined;
    /**
     * Validates a URL against an allowlist of schemes, returning the URL when
     * safe and `undefined` (with a dev warning) when not. Relative URLs always
     * pass; tab/newline/carriage-return characters are stripped before scheme
     * detection, mirroring browser URL parsing — this is what keeps `javascript:`
     * (and obfuscations like `java\tscript:`) out of `href`, `redirect`, and file
     * URL sinks. Without the module, URLs pass through unchecked.
     *
     * @param url The candidate URL (non-strings resolve to `undefined`).
     * @param schemes Lowercase schemes to allow, without the trailing colon.
     */
    sanitizeUrl: (url: unknown, schemes: string[]) => string | undefined;
    /**
     * Whether strings in the given area may render as HTML — pure
     * `$security.allowHtml` membership. A refusal renders the string escaped.
     * Sanitization is not this gate's concern: HTML that passes always renders
     * through `sanitizeHtml`.
     *
     * @param area The HTML area (`'content'`, `'grid'`, or `'slots'`).
     */
    allowsHtml: (area: SecurityHtmlArea) => boolean;
    /**
     * Whether a component name string may resolve to the globally registered
     * component of that name (`$security.allowComponents`). Warns once per name
     * in dev when it rejects. Callers consult it only for strings intended as
     * component names (explicit `component` / `template` / `layout` props, or
     * slot strings shaped like a component name), so a miss is always worth
     * surfacing.
     *
     * @param name The component name.
     */
    allowsComponent: (name: string) => boolean;
    /**
     * Whether an HTTP request URL is permitted by `$security.allowOrigins`.
     * Always `true` when the option is unset; purely relative URLs are always
     * allowed. Consulted by the HTTP module before sending any request.
     *
     * @param url The request URL, resolved or as passed to the HTTP module.
     */
    allowsOrigin: (url: string) => boolean;
    /**
     * Encrypts a value with the configured `$security.encrypt`, passing the
     * calling feature's purpose tag. Identity when no cipher is configured.
     *
     * @param value The plaintext value.
     * @param purpose The call-site tag (e.g. `'autosave:local'`).
     */
    encrypt: SecurityCipher;
    /**
     * Decrypts a value with the configured `$security.decrypt`, passing the
     * calling feature's purpose tag. Identity when no cipher is configured.
     *
     * @param value The stored value.
     * @param purpose The call-site tag (e.g. `'autosave:local'`).
     */
    decrypt: SecurityCipher;
}

//// modules/theme/types.d.ts
import type { CSSProperties, ComputedRef, MaybeRefOrGetter } from 'vue';
/**
 * Dark-mode configuration accepted by `createVueform` and the form-level
 * `darkMode` prop.
 *
 * - `'system'` — follows the OS preference via `prefers-color-scheme`.
 * - A CSS subselector string — watches `<html>` for a class or attribute.
 *   Examples: `'.dark'`, `'[data-theme="dark"]'`.

 * The theme module API. Owns token style generation and shared dark-mode
 * detection (CSS generation / injection happen at registration, not on the
 * instance).
 */

    /**
     * Creates a reactive `ComputedRef<CSSProperties>` from a `tokens` prop,
     * converting token keys to `--vf-*` CSS custom properties and applying
     * `tokens.dark` overrides when dark mode is active.
     *
     * An optional `dark` parameter explicitly forces dark (`true`) or light
     * (`false`) for this component's `tokens.dark` inline overrides. When
     * `undefined`, falls back to the global dark-mode detection.
     *
     * Must be called during component `setup()`.
     *
     * @param tokens The theme tokens object (or a getter/ref to one).
     * @param dark Optional explicit dark-mode override for this component.
     */
    makeTokens: (tokens: MaybeRefOrGetter<Record<string, any>>, dark?: MaybeRefOrGetter<boolean | undefined>) => ComputedRef<CSSProperties>;
}

//// modules/validation/createValidation.d.ts
import { type ComputedRef, type Ref } from 'vue';

import { type VueformInstance } from '../../helpers';

/**
 * Live bindings used to assemble a `ValidationOwner`.
 */
type MakeValidationOwnerOptions = {
    /**
     * Stable owner identity (units and views are keyed by it).
     */
    id: object;
    /**
     * Current element path getter.
     */
    path: () => string;
    /**
     * Current data path getter — where the owner's value lives in the model.
     * Store write notifications match owners by it; defaults to `path`.

    dataPath?: () => string;
    /**
     * The element (or virtual element) context getter.

    el$: () => StatefulElement;
    /**
     * Whether the source is translatable.
     */
    translatable: () => boolean;
    /**
     * Available language keys (only read when translatable).
     */
    languages: () => string[];
    /**
     * The raw value getter (full locale object for translatable sources).
     */
    value: () => any;
    /**
     * Whether to stop after the first failing unit of a language.
     */
    bail?: () => boolean;
    /**
     * Element-level debounce fallback.
     */
    debounce?: () => number;
    /**
     * Whether the owner has been touched (gates dependent revalidation).
     */
    touched?: () => boolean;
    /**
     * Whether the owner is currently available.
     */
    available?: () => boolean;
};
/**
 * Inputs for the element validation view-model. Everything is passed as live
 * bindings (refs / getters) so the view-model tracks the element's state
 * without owning it.
 */
type MakeElementValidationOptions = {
    /**
     * The parent form context, if any.
     */
    form$?: any;
    /**
     * Whether the element is the form root (validates the validation schema
     * instead of own rules).
     */
    isRoot: boolean;
    /**
     * The root model store, when the element is the form root (validator adoption
     * / attachment).
     */
    store?: object;
    /**
     * The element's own rules (`undefined` for the root).
     */
    rules: Ref<TRulesProp | undefined>;
    /**
     * The element's current path.
     */
    path: Ref<string>;
    /**
     * The element's current data path — where its value lives in the model. Store
     * write notifications match owners by it; defaults to `path`.
     */
    dataPath?: Ref<string>;
    /**
     * The element's raw model (full locale object for translatable elements).
     */
    model: Ref<any>;
    /**
     * The element's current-language value (validated by `validateCurrent`).
     */
    value: Ref<any>;
    /**
     * Available languages keyed by code.
     */
    languages: Ref<Record<string, any>>;
    /**
     * Whether the element is translatable.
     */
    translatable: Ref<boolean>;
    /**
     * The active language.
     */
    language: Ref<string>;
    /**
     * Whether the element has been touched (blurred at least once).
     */
    touched?: Ref<boolean | undefined>;
    /**
     * Whether the element is currently available.
     */
    available: Ref<boolean>;
    /**
     * Whether the element is a data container (containers with own rules watch
     * their model deeply).
     */
    isContainer: Ref<boolean>;
    /**
     * The resolved `validateOn` triggers (element prop with form fallback).
     */
    validateOn: Ref<string[] | undefined>;
    /**
     * The element's component context (`context$`), used as the owner's `el$`.
     */
    el$: () => StatefulElement;
    /**
     * Whether the element (including children) is invalid — the live-validation
     * policy keeps validating invalid elements so errors clear as they are fixed.
     * Lazy because the aggregate is derived from this view-model.
     */
    invalid: () => boolean;
    /**
     * Validates the element including children — what a user-input intent
     * triggers. Lazy for the same reason.
     */
    validate: () => Promise<boolean> | boolean;
};
/**
 * Inputs for the form validation view-model.
 */
type MakeFormValidationOptions = {
    /**
     * The form's validator (owned by the root element's view-model).
     */
    validator: Validator;
    /**
     * The resolved form-level Standard Schema (prop, `defineSchema` attachment,
     * or adopted model instance — resolution stays with the form).
     */
    validationSchema: Ref<StandardSchemaV1 | undefined>;
};
/**
 * Options for creating a validator (`getValidationModule().makeValidator` /
 * `createValidation(config).makeValidator`).
 */
type MakeValidatorOptions = {
    /**
     * The form data object model units validate.
     */
    model: Ref<unknown>;
    /**
     * The parent form context, if any.
     */
    form$?: FormContext;
    /**
     * The model store backing the validated model, when there is one. The
     * validator subscribes to its write notifications so every model mutation —
     * element input, `update()` / `load()` at any level, server write-backs —
     * dirties the validation schema and revalidates cross-field dependents,
     * without relying on call sites to notify. Duck-typed to avoid a module
     * dependency on the model package.
     */
    store?: {
        onWrite: (cb: (dataPath: string) => void) => () => void;
    };
    /**
     * Looks up an element by path (wildcard resolution, `$` params, model-unit
     * issue bucketing).
     *
     * @param path The element path to look up.
     */
    find: (path: string) => any;
    /**
     * How many times the form has been submitted (gates dependent revalidation).
     * A boolean `true` is treated as submitted (headless).
     */
    submits: () => number | boolean;
};
/**
 * Creates the validation module instance: validator creation, the element /
 * form view-models, owner assembly, store attachment, and the `validateOn`
 * policy.
 *
 * @param appConfig The resolved Vueform configuration (rule registry, message
 *   tags), used as the default config for validators.
 */
export declare function createValidation(vueform: VueformInstance): {
    makeValidator: (options: MakeValidatorOptions) => Validator;
    makeFormValidation: (options: MakeFormValidationOptions) => {
        issues: ComputedRef<Issue[]>;
        toStandardSchema: () => StandardSchemaV1<unknown, unknown>;
    };
    makeElementValidation: (options: MakeElementValidationOptions) => {
        validator: Validator;
        owner: ValidationOwner;
        validation: import("vue").ShallowReactive<Record<string, ValidationView>>;
        currentValidation: Readonly<Ref<ValidationView, ValidationView>>;
        hasOwnValidation: ComputedRef<boolean>;
        shouldValidate: ComputedRef<boolean>;
        success: ComputedRef<boolean>;
        required: ComputedRef<boolean>;
        invalidLanguages: ComputedRef<Set<string>>;
        ownInvalid: ComputedRef<boolean>;
        ownPending: ComputedRef<boolean>;
        ownDebouncing: ComputedRef<boolean>;
        ownValidated: ComputedRef<boolean>;
        ownRuleErrors: ComputedRef<string[]>;
        validateSelf: () => Promise<boolean>;
        validateCurrent: () => Promise<boolean>;
        invalidateSelf: () => void;
        unvalidateSelf: () => void;
        notifyChange: () => void;
        onUserInput: () => void;
        onBlur: () => void;
        initValidation: () => void;
        destroyValidation: () => void;
    };
    makeValidationOwner: (options: MakeValidationOwnerOptions) => ValidationOwner;
    attachValidator: (store: object, validator: Validator) => void;
    getAttachedValidator: (store: object) => Validator | undefined;
    toStandardSchema: (source: {
        toStandardSchema?: () => StandardSchemaV1;
    } | undefined) => StandardSchemaV1 | undefined;
    hasValidateOnTrigger: (validateOn: string[] | undefined, events: string | string[]) => boolean;
    shouldValidateLive: (input: {
        hasRules: boolean;
        validateOn: string[] | undefined;
        invalid: boolean;
        touched: boolean | undefined;
        form?: {
            validationDisabled: boolean;
            submitted: boolean;
        };
    }) => boolean;
    shouldValidateOnBlur: (input: {
        validateOn: string[] | undefined;
        submitted: boolean;
    }) => boolean;
};
export {};

/**
 * Returns the resolved instance's validation module, or the inert
 * `noopValidation` surface (everything valid) when the `validation` module is
 * not registered. Resolves the explicit `vueform` (a `createVueform()` instance
 * or config) when given, otherwise the config injected by the calling
 * component's app.

export declare function getValidationModule(vueform?: VueformInstance): ValidationModule;
