//// types/slots.d.ts
import type { ComponentRegistry } from './';
import type { Component } from 'vue';
/**
 * Maps component names to their accepted slot prop type.
 */
type ComponentsWithSlotsProp = {
    [K in keyof ComponentRegistry as keyof ComponentRegistry[K]['props'] extends never ? never : Extract<keyof ComponentRegistry[K]['props'], 'slots'> extends never ? never : K]: ComponentRegistry[K];
};
/**
 * Global slot override definitions, mapping component names to their available
 * slot names with replacement components.
 */
export type SlotsDefinition = {
    [K in keyof ComponentsWithSlotsProp]?: ComponentsWithSlotsProp[K] extends {
        slots: infer T extends Record<string, any>;
    } ? {
        [TK in keyof T]?: Component;
    } : never;
};
/**
 * Extracts the resolved slot prop types for every registered component, mapping
 * slot names to their prop shapes.
 */
export type SlotProps = {
    [K in keyof ComponentRegistry]: ComponentRegistry[K] extends {
        slots: infer T extends Record<string, any>;
    } ? {
        [TK in keyof T]: T[TK] extends () => any ? {} : T[TK] extends (props: infer P) => any ? P : never;
    } : never;
};
/**
 * Slot props of a possibly-unregistered component's slot. Same rationale as
 * `PartOf`: core types reference core-only components (`VfTabs`, `VfSteps`,
 * `VfLanguages`) whose registry augmentations are absent from adapter type
 * programs — degrade to a loose record instead of erroring.
 */
export type SlotPropsOf<C extends keyof SlotProps | (string & {}), S extends (C extends keyof SlotProps ? Extract<keyof SlotProps[C], string> : never) | (string & {})> = C extends keyof SlotProps ? S extends keyof SlotProps[C] ? SlotProps[C][S] : Record<string, any> : Record<string, any>;
export {};

//// types/standardSchema.d.ts
/**
 * Vendored Standard Schema V1 interface (https://standardschema.dev). The spec
 * is a types-only contract implemented by Zod (3.24+), Valibot, ArkType, and
 * others — vendoring it keeps core dependency-free while accepting any
 * spec-compliant schema in `rules` / `validationSchema`.
 */
export interface StandardSchemaV1<Input = unknown, Output = Input> {
    /**
     * The Standard Schema properties.
     */
    readonly '~standard': StandardSchemaV1.Props<Input, Output>;
}
export declare namespace StandardSchemaV1 {
    /**
     * The Standard Schema properties interface.
     */
    interface Props<Input = unknown, Output = Input> {
        /**
         * The version number of the standard.
         */
        readonly version: 1;
        /**
         * The vendor name of the schema library.
         */
        readonly vendor: string;
        /**
         * Validates unknown input values.
         */
        readonly validate: (value: unknown) => Result<Output> | Promise<Result<Output>>;
        /**
         * Inferred types associated with the schema (phantom, no runtime value).
         */
        readonly types?: Types<Input, Output> | undefined;
    }
    /**
     * The result interface of the validate function.
     */
    type Result<Output> = SuccessResult<Output> | FailureResult;
    /**
     * The result interface if validation succeeds.
     */
    interface SuccessResult<Output> {
        /**
         * The typed output value.
         */
        readonly value: Output;
        /**
         * The non-existent issues.
         */
        readonly issues?: undefined;
    }
    /**
     * The result interface if validation fails.
     */
    interface FailureResult {
        /**
         * The issues of failed validation.
         */
        readonly issues: readonly Issue[];
    }
    /**
     * The issue interface of the failure output.
     */
    interface Issue {
        /**
         * The error message of the issue.
         */
        readonly message: string;
        /**
         * The path of the issue, if any.
         */
        readonly path?: readonly (PropertyKey | PathSegment)[] | undefined;
    }
    /**
     * The path segment interface of the issue.
     */
    interface PathSegment {
        /**
         * The key representing a path segment.
         */
        readonly key: PropertyKey;
    }
    /**
     * The Standard Schema types interface.
     */
    interface Types<Input = unknown, Output = Input> {
        /**
         * The input type of the schema.
         */
        readonly input: Input;
        /**
         * The output type of the schema.
         */
        readonly output: Output;
    }
    /**
     * Infers the input type of a Standard Schema.
     */
    type InferInput<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1> = NonNullable<Schema['~standard']['types']>['input'];
    /**
     * Infers the output type of a Standard Schema.
     */
    type InferOutput<Schema extends StandardSchemaV1> = NonNullable<Schema['~standard']['types']>['output'];
}

//// types/theme.d.ts
/**
 * The shape of the `tokens` property accepted by `VueformConfig` and the
 * per-form / per-element `tokens` prop. Defaults to a loose record so core
 * remains visual-layer-agnostic. Adapter packages augment this interface via
 * declaration merging to restrict it to their known tokens.
 */
export interface ThemeTokens {
    [key: string]: any;
}
/**
 * Extracts all top-level token keys from a flat theme object, excluding the
 * reserved `dark` entry.
 */
export type ThemeTokenKeys<T> = Exclude<keyof T, 'dark'> & string;
/**
 * The exhaustive theme shape derived from a concrete theme definition: every
 * top-level token is **required**, and a `dark` override map must be present
 * (`{}` opts out of a dark variant). Adapters use this to type their
 * `defineTheme` helper so authoring a theme from scratch cannot silently omit
 * tokens — a missing or mistyped key surfaces as a type error.
 */
export type CompleteTheme<T extends Record<string, any>> = {
    [K in ThemeTokenKeys<T>]: string | number;
} & {
    dark: {
        [K in ThemeTokenKeys<T>]?: string | number;
    };
};
/**
 * Infers the `ThemeTokens` shape from a concrete theme map: every top-level
 * token key becomes optional, `dark` is surfaced as an override map, and
 * arbitrary custom keys stay accepted via the open index signature.
 *
 * This is what the adapters' `/themes` entries plug into the `ThemeTokens`
 * augmentation to make their token keys known to the editor — and what you use
 * to do the same for a custom-structure theme of your own:
 *
 * @example
 *   ;```ts
 *   declare module '\@vueform/core' {
 *     interface ThemeTokens extends InferThemeTokens<typeof myTheme> {}
 *   }
 *   ```
 */
export type InferThemeTokens<T extends Record<string, any>> = {
    [K in ThemeTokenKeys<T>]?: string | number;
} & {
    dark?: {
        [K in ThemeTokenKeys<T>]?: string | number;
    } & Record<string, string | number | undefined>;
    [key: string]: any;
};

//// types/utils.d.ts
import type { LooseContext } from './shared';
import type { Ref } from 'vue';
/**
 * Unwraps the inner composable from a `defineFeature` curried signature.
 */
type UnwrapFeature<F> = F extends (config?: any) => infer Next ? Next : F;
/**
 * Resolves the return type of a factory, including those created with
 * `defineFeature` which use a curried `(config?) => (options) => result`
 * signature.
 */
type FeatureReturn<F> = UnwrapFeature<F> extends (options: any) => infer R ? R : UnwrapFeature<F> extends (...args: any[]) => infer R ? R : never;
/**
 * Pairs a factory with keys to pick from its return type for `ReturnsOf`
 * aggregation.
 */
type Pair<Fn extends (...args: any) => any, Keys extends PropertyKey[]> = [
    Fn,
    Keys
];
/**
 * Extracts keys that are optional in the given type.
 */
type OptionalKeys<T> = {
    [K in keyof T]-?: {} extends Pick<T, K> ? K : never;
}[keyof T];
/**
 * Makes all keys required while preserving undefined in value unions.
 */
type RequirePropsButKeepUndefined<T> = Omit<Required<T>, OptionalKeys<T>> & {
    [K in OptionalKeys<T>]-?: Exclude<T[K], undefined> | undefined;
};
type CamelCaseJoin<S extends string> = S extends `${infer A}-${infer B}` ? CamelCaseJoin<`${A}${Capitalize<B>}`> : S extends `${infer A}_${infer B}` ? CamelCaseJoin<`${A}${Capitalize<B>}`> : S;
/**
 * Replaces the wide (constraint-instantiated) members of an Expose surface with
 * their narrow, prop-instantiated counterparts, for a component's `*Context`
 * interface:
 *
 * ```ts
 * NarrowExpose<VfSelectExpose, SelectApi<TProps>>
 * ```
 *
 * `TNarrow` is the prop-instantiated API slice (intersect multiple slices when
 * a component extension adds members). Its keys match the wide instantiation
 * carried by the Expose, so they double as the strip list. Stripping before
 * intersecting is required — otherwise wide and narrow members merge and e.g.
 * `Ref<any> & Ref<narrow>` collapses to `any`.
 */
export type NarrowExpose<TExpose, TNarrow extends Record<string, any>> = Omit<TExpose, keyof TNarrow> & TNarrow;
/**
 * Builds a component's plain (widest) props type from its generic props
 * interface and the blueprint's plain props:
 *
 * ```ts
 * type VfSelectProps = WidenProps<VfSelectProps, SelectProps>
 * ```
 *
 * Equals `TLoose & Omit<TProps, keyof TLoose>` — the blueprint's plain props
 * plus everything the component adds on top. Component-own props (e.g. `foo`)
 * stay visible to constraints / extensions without a separate `*OwnProps`
 * interface.
 *
 * Prefer this over a wide `TProps` instantiation as the constraint: component
 * props pin `*Context` via slots/context arguments, so constraining on them
 * makes `*Context`'s own type parameter resolve through the interface being
 * defined (order-dependent base-type cycle). The `Omit` only resolves member
 * _names_ of `TProps` plus the types of the added keys. Caveat: an added prop
 * typed with `*Context` / `*Slots` would reintroduce the cycle — keep own props
 * self-contained.
 */
export type WidenProps<TProps, TLoose> = TLoose & Omit<TProps, keyof TLoose>;
/**
 * `true` if `T` is `any`, otherwise `false`.
 */
export type IsAny<T> = 0 extends 1 & T ? true : false;
/**
 * Unwraps a single top-level `Ref` without distributing over unions.
 *
 * Vue's `ShallowUnwrapRef` uses a distributive `T extends Ref ? …` check, which
 * also peels `Ref` out of prop unions that list it as a member (e.g.
 * `PageProp`, `DProp`). Generic SFCs already expose some bindings unwrapped, so
 * applying distributive unwrap again would corrupt those unions. Wrapping the
 * check in a tuple keeps the condition non-distributive.
 */
export type UnwrapTopLevelRef<T> = [T] extends [Ref<infer V>] ? V : T;
/**
 * Unwraps a single top-level `Ref` per key without distributing over unions —
 * mirrors what `slotContext` / `ContextOf` produce for the component context.
 */
export type UnwrapApiRefs<T> = {
    [K in keyof T]: UnwrapTopLevelRef<T[K]>;
};
/**
 * Builds an event `context$` type from a blueprint factory: the factory's
 * return type (refs unwrapped) with the keys of `TGenerics` (model / items
 * fields) replaced by the component's generic-aware versions.
 *
 * Per-blueprint contexts must wrap this in an `interface` (e.g. `SelectContext
 * extends Context<typeof useBlueprint, …>`) so the blueprint type is resolved
 * lazily and does not cycle through the component registry.
 */
export type Context<TBlueprint extends (...args: any[]) => any, TGenerics> = Omit<UnwrapApiRefs<ReturnType<TBlueprint>>, keyof TGenerics> & TGenerics;
/**
 * Overlays generic API and props fields onto a component context for
 * `#template` slot typing.
 *
 * Widens `outlets` so the blueprint context (which carries the generic slot
 * map) stays assignable to the slot context type.
 *
 * Wrap the result in an `interface` at the component boundary so registry
 * cycles stay lazy.
 */
export type GenericContext<TContext extends {
    props: Record<string, any>;
}, TApi extends Record<string, any>, TProps extends Record<string, any>> = Omit<TContext, keyof TApi | 'props' | 'outlets'> & TApi & {
    outlets: Record<string, any>;
    props: Omit<TContext['props'], keyof TProps> & TProps;
};
/**
 * Remaps one event-tuple's args, replacing every `LooseContext` placeholder
 * with `Ctx`.
 */
export type RemapContextArgs<Args, Ctx> = {
    [I in keyof Args]: IsAny<Args[I]> extends true ? Args[I] : Args[I] extends LooseContext ? Ctx : Args[I];
};
/**
 * Reads an optional prop from a registry `TEntry` payload (schema entry / props
 * object), falling back to `undefined` when the key is absent.
 *
 * Using `prop?: infer V` on a type that lacks the prop yields `unknown`, which
 * poisons generic extraction (e.g. `groupChildren: unknown`). Keyof-gating
 * keeps missing props as `undefined`, matching SFC generic defaults.
 */
export type EntryPropOf<TEntry, K extends PropertyKey> = K extends keyof TEntry ? TEntry[K] : undefined;
/**
 * Reads an optional prop from a registry `TEntry` payload with a fallback
 * default applied when the key is absent or `undefined`.
 *
 * `any` passes through unchanged (instead of collapsing to the default via
 * `[any] extends [undefined]`) so wide registry instantiations stay maximally
 * permissive.
 */
export type EntryPropOr<TEntry, K extends PropertyKey, TDefault> = EntryPropOf<TEntry, K> extends infer V ? IsAny<V> extends true ? V : [V] extends [undefined] ? TDefault : V : TDefault;
/**
 * Unwraps a `Ref` wrapper that may appear on a registry entry's prop.
 */
export type UnwrapEntryRef<T> = T extends Ref<infer V> ? V : T;
/**
 * Widens a literal scalar to its primitive. Selection values follow the `items`
 * convention: const-narrowed schema literals must not lock the model.
 */
export type WidenScalar<T> = T extends string ? string : T extends number ? number : T extends boolean ? boolean : T;
/**
 * Simplifies a mapped or intersected type into a flat object type for better
 * IDE display.
 */
export type Prettify<T> = {
    [K in keyof T]: T[K];
} & {};
/**
 * Identity mapped type for generic function parameters (no `& {}`, unlike
 * `Prettify` — safe for large generic contexts).
 *
 * Property access on a value typed as a bare type parameter widens to the
 * constraint's apparent type (`api.items` on `TApi extends DropdownApi` yields
 * `DropdownApi['items']`). Access on a mapped type over the parameter resolves
 * to the indexed access instead (`TApi['items']`), so blueprint extensions can
 * return prop-narrowed API fields without return annotations or casts.
 */
export type Identity<T> = {
    [K in keyof T]: T[K];
};
/**
 * Converts a union type into an intersection by distributing over function
 * parameter positions.
 */
export type UnionToIntersection<U> = (U extends any ? (k: U) => void : never) extends (k: infer I) => void ? I : never;
/**
 * Joins two path segments with a dot separator, producing a template literal
 * type.
 */
export type Join<K, P> = K extends string | number | bigint ? P extends string | number | bigint ? `${K}.${P}` : never : never;
/**
 * Converts a kebab-case string to PascalCase at the type level.
 */
export type KebabToPascal<S extends string> = S extends `${infer Head}-${infer Tail}` ? `${Capitalize<Head>}${KebabToPascal<Tail>}` : Capitalize<S>;
/**
 * Recursively flattens nested arrays into their element type.
 */
export type FlattenDeep<T> = T extends readonly (infer U)[] ? FlattenDeep<U> : T;
/**
 * Picks and merges selected return-type keys from an array of `[function,
 * keys[]]` pairs into a single flat object. Keys selected via the second
 * argument `O` are merged as partial (optional) properties.
 */
export type ReturnsOf<P extends Pair<any, PropertyKey[]>[], O extends Pair<any, PropertyKey[]>[] = []> = Prettify<UnionToIntersection<{
    [I in keyof P]: P[I] extends Pair<infer F, infer K> ? PropertyKey extends keyof FeatureReturn<F> ? never : Pick<FeatureReturn<F>, Extract<K[number], keyof FeatureReturn<F>>> : never;
}[number] | {
    [I in keyof O]: O[I] extends Pair<infer F, infer K> ? PropertyKey extends keyof FeatureReturn<F> ? never : Partial<Pick<FeatureReturn<F>, Extract<K[number], keyof FeatureReturn<F>>>> : never;
}[number]>>;
/**
 * Makes all properties required while preserving `undefined` in the type of
 * originally optional properties.
 */
export type RequiredOrUndefined<T> = T extends object ? Prettify<RequirePropsButKeepUndefined<T>> : T;
/**
 * Makes the specified keys optional in a type while keeping the rest unchanged.
 */
export type MakeOptional<T, K extends PropertyKey> = T extends any ? K extends keyof T ? Omit<T, K> & Partial<Pick<T, K>> : T : never;
/**
 * Makes the specified keys required in a type while keeping the rest unchanged.
 */
export type MakeRequired<T, K extends PropertyKey> = T extends any ? K extends keyof T ? Omit<T, K> & Required<Pick<T, K>> : T : never;
/**
 * Camel-cases an identifier: lowers the first character and collapses `-` / `_`
 * separators (`update-model-value` → `updateModelValue`).
 */
export type CamelCase<S extends string> = CamelCaseJoin<Uncapitalize<S>>;
/**
 * Kebab-cases an identifier: a `-` is inserted before every uppercase
 * character, which is then lowered (`updateModelValue` →
 * `update-model-value`).
 */
export type KebabCase<S extends string> = S extends `${infer H}${infer T}` ? T extends Uncapitalize<T> ? `${Uncapitalize<H>}${KebabCase<T>}` : `${Uncapitalize<H>}-${KebabCase<T>}` : S;
/**
 * Extracts event names from a props type by finding `on`-prefixed keys and
 * converting them to camelCase and kebab-case.
 */
export type EventKeysFromProps<T> = keyof {
    [K in keyof T as K extends `on${infer E extends Capitalize<string>}` ? CamelCase<E> | KebabCase<E> : never]: any;
};
/**
 * Evaluates to `true` if the type `T` is a union, `false` if it is a single
 * type.
 */
export type IsUnion<T, U = T> = T extends any ? [U] extends [T] ? false : true : never;
/**
 * Like `Required<T>` but preserves the original property types without removing
 * `undefined`.
 */
export type LooseRequired<T> = {
    [P in keyof (T & Required<T>)]: T[P];
};
/**
 * Extracts keys from `T` whose value type is `boolean`.
 */
export type BooleanKey<T, K extends keyof T = keyof T> = K extends any ? T[K] extends boolean ? K : never : never;
/**
 * Merges two object types where keys from `E` override matching keys in `T`.
 */
export type SpreadMerge<T, E> = Omit<T, keyof E> & E;
/**
 * Wraps a type to allow either a single value or an array of that type.
 */
export type MaybeArray<T> = T | T[];
/**
 * Converts an emits interface into Vue-style `onEventName` prop functions.
 */
export type EmitsToProps<T> = {
    [K in string & keyof T as `on${Capitalize<K>}`]?: (...args: T[K] extends any[] ? T[K] : any[]) => any;
};
/**
 * Wraps a type to also accept a contextual function that receives the component
 * context and returns the value.
 *
 * @param context$ The component context passed when used as a function.
 */
export type MaybeContextual<T, TContext = any> = T | ((context$: TContext) => T | void);
/**
 * Replaces the `type` property of `T` with `any`, allowing any element type
 * string.
 */
export type WithAnyType<T> = Omit<T, 'type'> & {
    type?: any;
};
/**
 * Recursively makes all properties of an object type optional, while preserving
 * arrays as-is.
 */
export type DeepPartial<T> = T extends any[] ? T : T extends Record<string, any> ? {
    [K in keyof T]?: DeepPartial<T[K]>;
} : T;
/**
 * Makes all keys of `T` optional, while also making the members of keys in `K`
 * individually optional (one-level deep partial).
 */
export type PartialDeepKeys<T, K extends keyof T> = Partial<Omit<T, K>> & {
    [P in K]?: Partial<T[P]>;
};
/**
 * Makes specific keys `K` of `T` required while leaving the rest unchanged.
 */
export type RequireKeys<T, K extends keyof T> = T & Required<Pick<T, K>>;
/**
 * Makes an object type accept arbitrary extra string keys.
 */
export type OpenObject<T> = T extends Record<string, any> ? T & Record<string & {}, any> : T;
/**
 * Recursively makes all properties of an object type readonly, including nested
 * objects and arrays.
 */
export type DeepReadonly<T> = T extends (...args: any[]) => any ? T : T extends any[] ? ReadonlyArray<DeepReadonly<T[number]>> : T extends Record<string, any> ? {
    readonly [K in keyof T]: DeepReadonly<T[K]>;
} : T;
export {};

//// utils/array.d.ts
/**
 * Extracts the array portion from a type that may include non-array members.
 */
type ArrayPart<T> = Extract<NonNullable<T>, readonly any[]>;
/**
 * Checks whether an array type contains only string elements.
 */
type IsStringArray<T> = T extends readonly string[] ? true : false;
/**
 * Return type for converting values to array items.
 */
type ToArrayItemsReturn<TItems, TValueKey extends string, TLabelKey extends string> = [ArrayPart<TItems>] extends [never] ? Array<{
    [K in TValueKey]: string;
} & {
    [K in TLabelKey]: string;
}> : IsStringArray<ArrayPart<TItems>> extends true ? Array<{
    [K in TValueKey]: string;
} & {
    [K in TLabelKey]: string;
}> : ArrayPart<TItems>;
/**
 * Joins two values into an array, concatenating if either is already an array.
 *
 * @param a First value or array.
 * @param b Second value or array.
 */
export declare function joinMaybeArrays(a: any, b: any): any[];
/**
 * Wraps a value in an array if it is not already an array.
 *
 * @param input The value or array.
 */
export declare function toArray<T extends unknown>(input: T | T[]): T[];
/**
 * Converts an object or array of items into a normalized array format with
 * configurable value and label keys.
 *
 * @param items The items as a record or array.
 * @param valueKey The key name for values in the output array.
 * @param labelKey The key name for labels in the output array.
 */
export declare function toArrayItems<const TValueKey extends string = 'value', const TLabelKey extends string = 'label', TItems extends Record<string, string> | readonly string[] | readonly Record<string, any>[] | undefined = Record<string, string> | readonly string[] | readonly Record<string, any>[] | undefined>(items: TItems, valueKey?: TValueKey, labelKey?: TLabelKey): ToArrayItemsReturn<TItems, TValueKey, TLabelKey>;
/**
 * Returns a new array with an item moved from one index to another.
 *
 * @param array The source array.
 * @param fromIndex The index to move from.
 * @param toIndex The index to move to.
 */
export declare function move(array: any[], fromIndex: number | undefined, toIndex: number | undefined): any[];
export {};

//// utils/async.d.ts
import { type MaybeRef } from 'vue';
/**
 * Iterates over an array or object sequentially, awaiting each callback.
 *
 * @param arrayOrObject The collection to iterate over.
 * @param callback Async or sync callback invoked for each entry.
 */
export declare function asyncForEach<T>(arrayOrObject: Record<string, T> | T[], callback: (value: T, key: string | number, collection: Record<string, T> | T[]) => Promise<void> | void): Promise<void>;
/**
 * Type guard that checks whether a value is a thenable (has a `.then` method).
 *
 * @param value The value to test.
 */
export declare function isThenable<T>(value: T | PromiseLike<T>): value is PromiseLike<T>;
/**
 * Creates a debounced version of a function that delays invocation until after
 * the specified timeout. The returned function exposes a `cancel` method that
 * clears any pending invocation, which callers should invoke on teardown (e.g.
 * `onScopeDispose`) so a queued call cannot fire after disposal.
 *
 * @param func The function to debounce.
 * @param timeout Delay in milliseconds (supports reactive refs).
 */
export declare function debounce<TThis, TArgs extends unknown[], TResult>(func: (this: TThis, ...args: TArgs) => TResult, timeout: MaybeRef<string | number>): ((this: TThis, ...args: TArgs) => TResult | void) & {
    /**
     * Cancels any pending invocation, clearing the active debounce timer.
     */
    cancel: () => void;
};

//// utils/classes.d.ts
/**
 * Resolves refs anywhere inside a class value: the value itself, array members,
 * and the condition values of conditional objects. A functional class value is
 * wrapped so its result is resolved when it is called. Refs are read at resolve
 * time, so running inside a tracked computation (or a render effect, for
 * functions) keeps the resolved value reactive.
 *
 * @param value The class value to resolve.
 */
export declare function unrefClass(value: any): any;
/**
 * Merges two class values (strings, arrays, or functions) into a single
 * combined value.
 *
 * @param a The base class value.
 * @param b The class value to merge in.
 */
export declare function mergeClass(a: any, b: any): any;
/**
 * Merges a base classes record with an array of additions, combining values per
 * key.
 *
 * @param base The base classes record.
 * @param additions Array of class records to merge into the base.
 */
export declare function mergeClasses(base: Record<string, any>, additions: Record<string, any>[]): {
    [x: string]: any;
};

//// utils/color.d.ts
/**
 * RGB color representation.
 */
export interface RgbColor {
    r: number;
    g: number;
    b: number;
}
/**
 * HSB (Hue-Saturation-Brightness) color representation.
 */
export interface HsbColor {
    h: number;
    s: number;
    b: number;
}
/**
 * Supported color format identifiers.
 */
export type ColorFormat = (string & {}) | 'hex' | 'rgb' | 'hsb' | undefined;
/**
 * Maps a color format name to its value type.
 */
export type ColorValue<F extends ColorFormat> = F extends 'hex' ? string : F extends 'rgb' ? RgbColor : HsbColor;
/**
 * Converts a hex color string to an RGB object.
 *
 * @param hex Hex string, with or without a leading `#`.
 */
export declare function hexToRgb(hex: string): RgbColor;
/**
 * Converts an RGB object to a 6-character hex string (no `#` prefix).
 *
 * @param rgb The RGB color to convert.
 */
export declare function rgbToHex(rgb: RgbColor): string;
/**
 * Converts an RGB object to an HSB object (h: 0–360, s: 0–100, b: 0–100).
 *
 * @param rgb The RGB color to convert.
 */
export declare function rgbToHsb(rgb: RgbColor): HsbColor;
/**
 * Converts an HSB object (h: 0–360, s: 0–100, b: 0–100) to an RGB object.
 *
 * @param hsb The HSB color to convert.
 */
export declare function hsbToRgb(hsb: HsbColor): RgbColor;
/**
 * Converts a color value from one format to another. Returns the value
 * unchanged if the formats are the same or the value is nullish.
 *
 * @param value The source color value.
 * @param newFormat The target color format.
 * @param oldFormat The source color format.
 */
export declare function convertColor(value: any, newFormat: ColorFormat, oldFormat: ColorFormat): any;

/**
 * Whether the build runs in production mode. A function, not a module-level
 * constant: the flag is read at call time, so behavior that depends on it (e.g.
 * the security module's fail-closed misconfiguration handling) follows the
 * environment the moment it runs — which is also what lets tests exercise
 * production behavior via `vi.stubEnv`. Bundlers still substitute
 * `process.env.NODE_ENV` inside this module, so production builds fold the body
 * to a constant.
 */
export declare function isProd(): boolean;
/**
 * The inverse of `isProd` — development (and test) mode, where dev warnings
 * fire and misconfigured states stay permissive.
 */
export declare function isDev(): boolean;

export declare function isFileValue(value: any): value is File | Blob;

 * Serializes a plain data object into a `FormData` instance using PHP-style

 * they have no rows or only empty rows; objects when all values are empty.

export declare function isEmptyValue(value: any, nullNode: any): boolean;

//// utils/instance.d.ts
import { type ComponentInternalInstance, type Slot } from 'vue';
import type { ComponentOptions } from '../types';
/**
 * A dynamic props source in a Vapor instance's `rawProps.$` array: either a
 * resolver function returning a props object (e.g. a compiled `v-bind` spread)
 * or a plain props object.
 */
type DynamicPropsSource = (() => Record<string, unknown>) | Record<string, unknown>;
/**
 * Structural type for Vue 3.6+ Vapor component instances. Vue does not publicly
 * export `VaporComponentInstance`, so this mirrors the fields Vueform relies
 * on. Vapor instances have no `vnode` and no `proxy`.
 */
export interface VaporInstanceLike {
    /**
     * Discriminant flag set by the Vapor runtime on every vapor instance.
     */
    vapor: true;
    /**
     * The instance's unique id.
     */
    uid: number;
    /**
     * The component definition, including fields merged from `defineOptions`
     * (e.g. `name`, `element`).
     */
    type: Record<string, any>;
    /**
     * The raw props passed to the component: static keys live directly on the
     * object (values may be compiler-generated getters), dynamic spread sources
     * live under `$`.
     */
    rawProps: Record<string, unknown> & {
        $?: DynamicPropsSource[];
    };
    /**
     * The resolved, reactive props object.
     */
    props: Record<string, any>;
    /**
     * The resolved, reactive fallthrough attrs object.
     */
    attrs: Record<string, any>;
    /**
     * The object registered via `expose()`, if any.
     */
    exposed: Record<string, any> | null;
    /**
     * The rendered block: a DOM node, a fragment (`{ nodes }`), a child vapor
     * component instance, or an array of these.
     */
    block?: unknown;
    /**
     * The app context shared with the VDOM world.
     */
    appContext: ComponentInternalInstance['appContext'];
    /**
     * Emits a component event.
     */
    emit: (event: string, ...args: any[]) => void;
}
/**
 * A component instance in either rendering mode: a VDOM
 * `ComponentInternalInstance` or a Vapor instance.
 */
export type GenericInstance = ComponentInternalInstance | VaporInstanceLike;
/**
 * Returns whether the given instance is a Vapor component instance.
 *
 * @param vm The instance to check.
 */
export declare function isVaporInstance(vm: GenericInstance | null | undefined): vm is VaporInstanceLike;
/**
 * Returns the current component instance in either rendering mode: inside a
 * Vapor component's setup on Vue 3.6+ the Vapor instance, otherwise the VDOM
 * instance from `getCurrentInstance()`. Returns `null` outside setup context.
 *
 * The vapor `currentInstance` binding is checked first because on 3.6
 * `getCurrentInstance()` skips vapor instances and falls back to
 * `currentRenderingInstance`, which inside a vapor-rendered tree points at the
 * subtree root rather than the current component.
 */
export declare function getGenericInstance(): GenericInstance | null;
/**
 * Returns the component definition (name, element flag, props, emits) for an
 * instance in either rendering mode. On VDOM instances this is the merged
 * `$options` view when a proxy exists (preserving mixin/extends semantics);
 * otherwise the raw component `type`.
 *
 * @param vm The component instance.
 */
export declare function getComponentDef(vm: GenericInstance): ComponentOptions;
/**
 * Wraps a raw Vapor slot function (which returns DOM blocks) into a
 * VDOM-renderable slot function returning VNodes, so it can be rendered with
 * `h()`, `<component :is>`, or called directly by VDOM code. Mirrors the
 * wrapping the vapor interop's slots proxy applies when a VDOM component
 * receives slots from a vapor parent: Vue 3.6's `renderSlot` renders slot
 * functions marked as vapor slots through a `VaporSlot` interop block.
 *
 * Only call this for slots of a Vapor instance — VDOM slot functions must be
 * passed through untouched.
 *
 * @param name The slot name.
 * @param slot The raw Vapor slot function.
 */
export declare function toVdomRenderableSlot(name: string, slot: Slot): Slot;
/**
 * Returns the root DOM node of a component instance in either rendering mode:
 * the VDOM `$el` (which may be a text/comment node for fragment roots) or the
 * first node of a Vapor instance's block. Returns `null` before mount.
 *
 * @param vm The component instance.
 */
export declare function getInstanceRootNode(vm: GenericInstance): Node | null;
/**
 * Returns the raw prop keys passed to a component instance (explicitly passed
 * props, listeners, and fallthrough attrs) in either rendering mode. For Vapor
 * instances this includes keys from resolved dynamic spread sources.
 *
 * @param vm The component instance.
 */
export declare function getInstanceRawPropKeys(vm: GenericInstance): string[];
/**
 * Returns whether an exact raw prop key was explicitly passed to a component
 * instance, in either rendering mode. No camelCase/kebab-case conversion is
 * performed — callers check both variants when needed. Mirrors the Vapor
 * runtime's `hasAttrFromRawProps` for Vapor instances.
 *
 * @param vm The component instance.
 * @param key The exact raw prop key to check.
 */
export declare function hasInstanceRawProp(vm: GenericInstance, key: string): boolean;
/**
 * Returns whether a raw prop was explicitly passed to a component instance by
 * camelCase or kebab-case name, in either rendering mode. Mirrors the variant
 * handling of `hasRawProp` for raw props objects.
 *
 * @param vm The component instance.
 * @param key The prop name to check (any casing).
 */
export declare function hasInstanceRawPropLoose(vm: GenericInstance, key: string): boolean;
/**
 * Returns the raw value of an exact prop key passed to a component instance, in
 * either rendering mode. Dynamic spread sources take precedence over static
 * keys (last source wins), mirroring the Vapor runtime's `getAttrFromRawProps`
 * (without its `class`/`style` merging, which Vueform never reads through this
 * path).
 *
 * @param vm The component instance.
 * @param key The exact raw prop key to read.
 */
export declare function getInstanceRawProp(vm: GenericInstance, key: string): unknown;
export {};

 * @param active Whether normalization is active (pass `false` to return the
 *   value as-is).
 */
export declare function normalize(value: any, active?: boolean): any;

export declare function normalizePreset(value: PresetDefinition): NormalizedPresetDefinition[];

//// utils/object.d.ts
/**
 * A plain object with string keys and unknown values.
 */
type PlainObj = Record<string, unknown>;
/**
 * Checks whether a value is a plain object (not an array, Date, RegExp, File,
 * etc.).
 *
 * @param value The value to test.
 */
export declare function isPlainObject(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown>;
/**
 * Deep clones a value, supporting primitives, Date, File, arrays, and plain
 * objects.
 *
 * @param value The value to clone.
 */
export declare function clone<T>(value: T): T;
/**
 * Deep equality check. Uses recursive comparison for objects and arrays,
 * falling back to strict equality for primitives.
 *
 * @param a First value.
 * @param b Second value.
 */
export declare function equals(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean;
/**
 * Type-safe wrapper around `Object.entries` that preserves key and value types.
 *
 * @param obj The object to extract entries from.
 */
export declare function typedEntries<T extends object, K extends keyof T>(obj?: T): [K, T[K]][];
/**
 * Type-safe wrapper around `Object.keys` that returns typed key array.
 *
 * @param o The object to extract keys from.
 */
export declare function typedKeys<T extends object>(o: T): Array<keyof T>;
/**
 * Returns the first argument that is not `undefined`.
 *
 * @param args Values to coalesce.
 */
export declare function coalesce(...args: any[]): any;
/**
 * Checks whether a raw props object contains a property by camelCase or
 * kebab-case name.
 *
 * @param raw The raw props object.
 * @param key The property name to check.
 */
export declare function hasRawProp(raw: Record<string, any>, key: string): boolean;
/**
 * Whether a plain object is a Vue component definition — a compiled SFC or a
 * `defineComponent` result — as opposed to a data object. Such values must be
 * treated atomically by prop merging: merging two definitions' keys produces a
 * broken hybrid component.
 *
 * @param value The plain object to test.
 */
export declare function isComponentDefinition(value: Record<string, unknown>): boolean;
/**
 * Merges two prop values with special handling for `classes` and `presets`.
 * Plain objects merge shallowly, except component definitions (a `template`,
 * `layout`, or slot component), which replace as a whole.
 *
 * @param a The base value.
 * @param b The overriding value.
 * @param prop The property name (used for special merge strategies).
 * @param merge Whether to merge or replace.
 */
export declare function mergeProp(a: any, b: any, prop: string, merge?: boolean): any;
/**
 * Deeply merges two plain objects up to a maximum nesting depth.
 *
 * @param target The base object.
 * @param source The source object to merge in.
 * @param maxDepth Maximum recursion depth for merging nested objects.
 */
export declare function mergeUntilDepth<T extends PlainObj, U extends PlainObj>(target: T, source: U, maxDepth?: number): T & U;
/**
 * Recursively merges `data` into `current`: when both are plain objects their
 * keys are merged, otherwise `data` overrides `current`.
 *
 * @param current The existing value to merge into.
 * @param data The incoming value to merge or override with.
 */
export declare function mergeOrReplace(current: any, data: any): any;
/**
 * Deeply merges multiple source objects into a target with unlimited depth.
 * Plain objects are recursively merged, arrays are concatenated, and all other
 * values are overwritten by the last source that defines them.
 *
 * @param target The base object to merge into (not mutated).
 * @param sources One or more source objects to merge from left to right.
 */
export declare function merge<T extends PlainObj>(target: T, ...sources: PlainObj[]): T;
/**
 * Reads a property as an **own** property only: the value when the object
 * carries the key itself, `undefined` otherwise — the prototype chain never
 * answers. Use it wherever an untrusted or semi-trusted string indexes into an
 * object (config policy flags, rule registries): an inherited value from a
 * polluted `Object.prototype` (via a pollution bug in any other library on the
 * page) must never satisfy the read.
 *
 * @param obj The object to read from.
 * @param key The property key.
 */
export declare function own<T extends object, K extends keyof T>(obj: T, key: K): T[K] | undefined;
export {};

//// utils/path.d.ts
/**
 * Result of splitting a dot-notation path into its first segment and remainder.
 */
type PathSplit = {
    before: string;
    index: number;
    after?: string;
};
/**
 * Replaces `.*` wildcard segments in a path with numeric indices extracted from
 * a fill path.
 *
 * @param fillable The path containing `.*` wildcards.
 * @param fill The concrete path whose numeric segments fill the wildcards.
 */
export declare function replaceWildcards(fillable: string, fill: string): string;
/**
 * Replaces `[*]` wildcard segments in an expression path with numeric indices
 * from a fill path.
 *
 * @param fillable The expression path containing `[*]` wildcards.
 * @param fill The concrete path whose numeric segments fill the wildcards.
 * @param brackets Whether to use bracket notation (`[n]`) or dot notation
 *   (`.n`).
 */
export declare function replaceWildcardsExpr(fillable: string, fill: string, brackets?: boolean): string;
/**
 * Splits a dot-separated path at the last numeric index segment.
 *
 * @param path The dot-separated path to split.
 */
export declare function splitByLastIndex(path: string): PathSplit | undefined;
/**
 * Retrieves a deeply nested value from an object or array using a dot-separated
 * path.
 *
 * @param obj The source object or array.
 * @param path Dot-separated path or array of keys.
 * @param defaultValue Value returned when the path does not resolve.
 */
export declare function get(obj: Record<string, any> | any[], path: string | string[], defaultValue?: any): any;
/**
 * Sets a deeply nested value in an object or array using a dot-separated path,
 * creating intermediate containers as needed.
 *
 * @param obj The target object or array.
 * @param path Dot-separated path or array of keys.
 * @param value The value to set.
 */
export declare function set(obj: Record<string, any> | any[], path: string | string[], value: any): Record<string, any> | any[];
/**
 * Removes a deeply nested value from an object or array using a dot-separated
 * path.
 *
 * @param obj The target object or array.
 * @param path Dot-separated path or array of keys.
 */
export declare function unset(obj: Record<string, any> | any[], path: string | string[]): boolean;
export {};

//// utils/schema.d.ts
import type { FormSchema } from '../types';
/**
 * Normalizes a form schema (array or object notation) into `[name, props]`
 * entries, mirroring `useSchema`'s resolution without component naming.
 *
 * @param schema The form schema in either notation.
 */
export declare function schemaEntries(schema: FormSchema | undefined): [string, Record<string, any>][];

//// utils/string.d.ts
import type { KebabToPascal } from '../types';
/**
 * Converts a string to camelCase.
 *
 * @param str The input string.
 */
export declare function toCamelCase(str: string): string;
/**
 * Converts a string to PascalCase.
 *
 * @param str The input string.
 */
export declare function toPascalCase(str: string): string;
/**
 * Converts a string to kebab-case.
 *
 * @param str The input string.
 */
export declare function toKebabCase(str: string): string;
/**
 * Converts a camelCase string to kebab-case.
 *
 * @param str The camelCase input string.
 */
export declare function camelToKebab(str: string): string;
/**
 * Converts a kebab-case string to PascalCase with typed return.
 *
 * @param input The kebab-case input string.
 */
export declare function kebabToPascal<T extends string>(input: T): KebabToPascal<T>;
/**
 * Capitalizes the first character of a string.
 *
 * @param str The input string.
 */
export declare function upperFirst<T extends string>(str: T): Capitalize<T>;
/**
 * Uncapitalizes the first character of a string.
 *
 * @param str The input string.
 */
export declare function lowerFirst<T extends string>(str: T): Uncapitalize<T>;
/**
 * Escapes regex metacharacters so a string can be embedded in a `RegExp`
 * pattern literally.
 *
 * @param str The string to escape.
 */
export declare function escapeRegExp(str: string): string;
/**
 * Parses a regex string in `/pattern/flags` format into a `RegExp` object.
 *
 * @param str The regex string to parse.
 */
export declare function stringToRegex(str: string): RegExp;
/**
 * Whether a string contains markup an HTML parser would act on. Aligned with
 * the parser's own rule: `<` opens markup only when followed by a tag-start
 * character — a letter (element), `/` (closing tag), `!` (comment/doctype) or
 * `?` (bogus comment). A comparison like `score < 10` stays plain text, while
 * `a<b` genuinely opens a `<b>` element and is correctly flagged. Used to
 * decide whether a resolved string needs the sanitizer / HTML rendering at all
 * — plain text never should.
 *
 * @param value The string to test.
 */
export declare function containsHtml(value: string): boolean;

//// utils/vue.d.ts
import { type ComputedGetter, type ComputedRef, type MaybeRef, type Ref } from 'vue';
import type { VueformRouter } from '../modules/router';
/**
 * Shared constant computed that always resolves to `true`. Reuse it for
 * fallback/stub paths instead of allocating a `computed(() => true)` per call
 * site.
 */
export declare const alwaysTrue: ComputedRef<boolean>;
/**
 * Shared constant computed that always resolves to `false`. Reuse it for
 * fallback/stub paths instead of allocating a `computed(() => false)` per call
 * site.
 */
export declare const alwaysFalse: ComputedRef<boolean>;
/**
 * Shared constant computed that always resolves to an empty array. Reuse it for
 * fallback/stub paths instead of allocating a `computed(() => [])` per call
 * site.
 */
export declare const emptyArray: ComputedRef<any[]>;
/**
 * Shared constant computed that always resolves to an empty language set. Reuse
 * it for fallback/stub paths instead of allocating a `computed(() => new
 * Set())` per call site.
 */
export declare const emptyLanguages: ComputedRef<Set<string>>;
/**
 * The result of aliasing property names on a source type. Alias keys replace
 * their corresponding source keys, and all un-aliased source keys pass
 * through.
 */
type AliasedProps<T extends Record<string, any>, A extends Record<string, keyof T & string>> = {
    [K in keyof A]: T[A[K] & keyof T];
} & T;
/**
 * Returns a `computed` that is not allocated until `.value` is first read. The
 * inner computed is created in the effect scope active at call time, so it is
 * disposed with that scope even if the first read happens later.
 *
 * Vue's `computed` is already lazy on evaluation; this is lazy on allocation.
 *
 * @param getter The computed getter.
 */
export declare function lazyComputed<T>(getter: ComputedGetter<T>): ComputedRef<T>;
/**
 * Creates a record of `Ref`s by picking the specified keys from an object using
 * `toRef`.
 *
 * @param object The source reactive object.
 * @param pick Keys to pick from the object.
 */
export declare function pickRefs<T extends Record<string, any>, P extends keyof T & string>(object: T, pick: P[]): { [K in P]: Ref<T[K], T[K]>; };
/**
 * Lazy `toRef` proxy over a reactive props object. Property access returns a
 * cached `Ref` for that key, so destructuring is reactive: `const { multiple }
 * = api.propRefs`.
 *
 * @param props The resolved props object (e.g. from `useProps`).
 */
export declare function createPropRefs<T extends Record<string, any>>(props: T): { [K in keyof T]-?: Ref<T[K], T[K]>; };
/**
 * Resolves `props:<target>` bindings from props, merging class values with the
 * base.
 *
 * @param props The component's raw props.
 * @param target The target part name (looked up as `props:<target>`).
 * @param base Optional base props to merge into.
 */
export declare function withDefaultProps(props: Record<string, any>, target: string, base?: Record<string, any>): any;
/**
 * Creates a proxy over a reactive props object that exposes aliased property
 * names. Reads are redirected through the original reactive source, preserving
 * Vue's reactivity tracking without introducing an intermediate reactive
 * wrapper (which would break with inline array/object props that create new
 * references on every render).
 *
 * @param source The reactive props object (e.g. from `useProps`).
 * @param aliases A mapping from desired alias key to original source key.
 */
export declare function aliasProps<T extends Record<string, any>, const A extends Record<string, keyof T & string>>(source: T, aliases: A): AliasedProps<T, A>;
/**
 * Resolves a vue-router instance from the Vueform config or the Vue app's
 * global `$router` property. Returns `undefined` when the config explicitly
 * disables the router (`false`) or no router is available.
 */
export declare function resolveRouter(configRouter: VueformRouter | false | undefined): VueformRouter | undefined;
/**
 * Converts a ref of an object into a reactive-like proxy whose property reads
 * and writes are forwarded to the current ref value (nested refs unwrapped on
 * read). Replacing the ref's value is reflected on the proxy immediately.
 */
export declare function toReactive<T extends object>(objectRef: MaybeRef<T>): T;
/**
 * A computed whose object result is exposed as a reactive-like proxy, so
 * property access stays reactive without `.value` (equivalent to
 * `toReactive(computed(fn))`).
 */
export declare function reactiveComputed<T extends object>(fn: () => T): T;
export {};

//// utils/walkCells.d.ts
import type { ResolvedCell, ResolvedGrid } from '../blueprints/grid';
/**
 * Iterates over every cell in a resolved grid, computing rowspan/colspan and
 * padded indices while tracking occupied cells.
 *
 * @param grid The resolved grid structure.
 * @param callback Callback invoked for each cell with positional and span
 *   metadata.
 */
export declare function walkCells(grid: ResolvedGrid, callback: ({ cell, }: {
    cell: ResolvedGrid[number][number];
    field: ResolvedCell | null;
    rowspan: number;
    colspan: number;
    rowIndex: number;
    colIndex: number;
    rowStart: number;
    colStart: number;
    rowEnd: number;
    colEnd: number;
    paddedColIndex: number;
}) => void): void;

//// utils/warn.d.ts
/**
 * Emits a framework warning with the standard `[Vueform warn]: ` prefix, so
 * every warning is greppable and consistently branded. Call sites keep their
 * own `isDev()` guards — the guard stays inline so bundlers can drop the entire
 * branch (message strings included) from production builds.
 *
 * @param message The warning message, without the prefix.
 * @param args Extra values forwarded to `console.warn` (e.g. an error).
 */
export declare function warn(message: string, ...args: unknown[]): void;
